1
自古后族，能以德禮進退、全宗保名者，鮮矣。 蓋恃宮掖之寵，接宴私之歡，高爵厚祿驕其內，聲色服玩惑於外； 莫知師友之訓，不達危亡之道。 故以中才處之，罕不覆敗； 亦由重植之木，自然顛披也。 明哲之君，知驕侈之易滿，榮寵之難保； 授任各當其才，祿位不過其量； 告之以天命不易，誡之以大義滅親； 使居無過之地，永享不貲之福，與國終始，不失其所以親也。 《易》曰：「震來虩虩，恐致福也。 」又曰：「婦子嘻嘻，失家節也。 」與其愛而失節，曷若懼而致福？ 魏氏懲漢人之敗，著矯枉之法：幼主嗣位，母后不得臨朝； 外氏無功，時主不得封爵。 雖曰刻薄，而卞、甄之族，竟無大過。 皇唐受命，長孫、竇氏以勛賢任職，而武氏、韋氏以盈滿致覆。 夫廢興者，豈天命哉，蓋人事也！ 竇威、長孫無忌各自有傳，其餘載其得失，為《外戚傳》，以存鑒誡焉。
Since antiquity, few among empresses' kin have managed to conduct themselves with virtue and propriety, stepping forward or back as circumstances required, and so preserve both clan and renown. They rely on favor within the inner palace and the pleasures of private feasts; lofty titles and rich stipends feed their pride, while sensual delights, fine attire, and luxuries distract them without. They heed neither the counsel of teachers nor friends, and never learn the road to ruin. Hence even those of moderate ability, once placed in such positions, rarely escape destruction. It is like a tree burdened with too heavy a crown — it must sooner or later topple. A wise ruler knows that arrogance and excess soon run their course, and that honor and favor are hard to hold. He appoints each man to a post fitting his ability and never grants salary or rank beyond his measure. He teaches them that Heaven's mandate is not trifled with and warns them that the greater principle may require sacrificing even one's own kin. So they stand blameless, enjoy lasting fortune beyond measure, and remain bound to the dynasty to the end without forfeiting the grounds of their intimacy with the throne. The Book of Changes says: "When Thunder comes, fearful and fearful — through fear one may attain blessing." It also says: "The wife and child laughing and laughing — this is the loss of household discipline." Better to foster fear and attain blessing than to indulge with love and lose discipline? The Wei, taking warning from the Han collapse, established corrective laws: when a young sovereign succeeded, the empress dowager might not preside over court. Maternal kin without merit might not be enfeoffed by the reigning sovereign. Though the laws were called harsh, the Bian and Zhen clans never in the end committed great offenses. When Tang received the Mandate, the Zhangsun and Dou clans served through merit and virtue, whereas the Wu and Wei clans were ruined through excess and overreach. As for rise and fall — is it the Mandate of Heaven? It is human affairs! Dou Wei and Zhangsun Wuji each has his own biography; the rest are recorded here for their successes and failures in these Biographies of Empress Consorts' Relatives, to preserve them as a warning.
2
=獨孤懷恩=
Dugu Huai'en
3
獨孤懷恩，元貞皇后弟之子也。 父整，隋涿郡太守。 懷恩幼時，以獻皇后之侄，養於宮中。 後仕為鄠縣令。 高祖平京城，授長安令。 在職嚴明，甚得時譽。 及高祖受禪，擢拜工部尚書。 時虞州刺史韋義節擊堯君素於蒲州，而義節文吏怯懦，頻戰不利。 高祖遣懷恩代總其眾。 懷恩督兵城下，為賊所拒，頻戰不利。 高祖切讓之，因是怨望。 高祖嘗戲之曰：「弟姑子悉為天子，次當舅子乎？ 」懷恩遂自以為符命，每扼腕曰：「我家豈女獨富貴耶？ 」由是陰圖異計。
Dugu Huai'en was the son of Empress Yuan Zhen's younger brother. His father Zheng was governor of Zhuo commandery under the Sui. In his youth, as nephew of Empress Xian, Huai'en was raised in the palace. Later he served as magistrate of E county. When Gaozu pacified the capital region, he was appointed magistrate of Chang'an. In office he was strict and fair-minded and won great repute. When Gaozu received the abdication, Huai'en was promoted to Minister of Works. At that time Wei Yijie, prefect of Yuzhou, was attacking Yao Junsu at Pu province, but Yijie, a civil official and a coward, repeatedly fought without success. Gaozu sent Huai'en to replace him and take overall command of the army. Huai'en led troops beneath the walls but was repulsed by the rebels and repeatedly fought without success. Gaozu sharply rebuked him, and he therefore harbored resentment. Gaozu once joked with him: "The sons of my sisters-in-law have all become emperors — is it next the turn of the son of my wife's brother?" Huai'en then took this as a sign of destiny; he often clutched his wrist and said: "Is my house alone to be denied wealth and honor because it has a woman?" Thereupon he secretly plotted treason.
4
時虞鄉南山多群盜。 劉武周將宋金剛寇陷澮州，高祖悉發關中卒以隸太宗，屯於柏壁。 懷恩遂與解縣令榮靜、前五原縣主簿元君寶謀引王行本兵及武周連和，與山賊劫永豐倉而斷柏壁糧道，割河東地以啗武周。 事臨發，會夏縣人呂崇茂殺縣令，據縣起兵，應武周。 高祖遣懷恩與永安王孝基、陜州總管於筠、內史侍郎唐儉攻崇茂。 宋金剛潛兵來襲，諸將盡沒。 君寶與開府劉讓亦同陷於賊中，遂泄懷恩之謀。 既而懷恩逃歸，高祖復令率師攻蒲州。 唐儉在賊中，說賊將尉遲敬德，請使讓還，連和罷兵，遂使發其事。 會堯君素為其下所殺，小帥王行本以蒲州降，懷恩勒兵入據其城。 高祖將濟河，已御舟矣，會讓至，乃使召懷恩，懷恩不知事已泄，輕舟來赴。 及中流而執之，收其黨按驗，遂誅之，時年三十六，籍沒基家。
At that time there were many bandits in the southern mountains of Yuxiang. Liu Wuzhou's general Song Jingang invaded and captured Fen province; Gaozu mobilized all the troops of Guanzhong under Taizong, who encamped at Baiyu. Huai'en then conspired with Rong Jing, magistrate of Jie county, and Yuan Junbao, former chief clerk of Wuyuan county, to bring Wang Xingben's troops and Liu Wuzhou into alliance, join with the mountain bandits to raid the Yongfeng granary and cut Baiyu's supply line, and cede the lands east of the River to bribe Liu Wuzhou. When the plot was about to be launched, Lü Chongmao of Xia county killed the magistrate, seized the county, and raised troops in support of Liu Wuzhou. Gaozu sent Huai'en together with Prince Yong'an Xiaoji, Area Commander of Shan province Yu Jun, and Secretariat Vice-Director Tang Jian to attack Chongmao. Song Jingang secretly led troops to raid them, and all the generals were destroyed. Junbao and Palace Director Liu Rang were likewise captured by the enemy and there revealed Huai'en's plot. Shortly afterward Huai'en fled back, and Gaozu again ordered him to lead troops to attack Pu province. Tang Jian, who was among the enemy, persuaded the rebel general Yuchi Jingde to request Liu Rang's return and a pact to cease fighting, and thereby had the affair exposed. When Yao Junsu was killed by his subordinates and junior commander Wang Xingben surrendered Pu province, Huai'en led troops in and seized the city. Gaozu was about to cross the river and had already boarded his boat when Liu Rang arrived; he therefore sent to summon Huai'en, who did not know the matter had been exposed and came lightly in a small boat. Midstream he was seized; his accomplices were arrested and examined, and he was executed. He was thirty-six. His family's property was confiscated.
5
=竇德明=
Dou Deming
6
竇德明，太穆順聖皇后兄之孫也。 祖照，尚後魏文帝女義陽公主，封鉅鹿公。 父彥，襲父封，仕隋為西平郡守。 德明少師事陳留王孝逸，頗涉文史。 會漢王諒作亂，遣其將綦良攻黎州。 德明時年十八，募得五千人，倍道而進，號令嚴整，一戰破之。 以功累拜齊王府屬，坐事免。 及義師圍長安，永安王孝基、襄邑王神符、江夏王道宗及高祖之婿竇誕、趙慈景並繫獄，隋將衛文升、陰世師欲殺之。 德明謂文升曰：「罪不在此輩，殺之無傷於彼，適足招怨。 」文升乃止。 及謁見高祖，竟不自言，時人稱其長者。 武德初，拜考功郎中。 從太宗擊王世充，頻有戰功，封顯武男。 貞觀初，歷常、愛二州刺史。 尋卒。
Dou Deming was the grandson of Empress Taimu Shunsheng's elder brother. His grandfather Zhao married Princess Yiyang, daughter of Emperor Wen of Later Wei, and was enfeoffed as Duke of Julu. His father Yan inherited his father's title and served the Sui as governor of Xiping commandery. In youth Deming studied under Wang Xiaoyi of Chenliu and gained considerable knowledge of literature and history. When Prince Han Liang rebelled, he sent his general Qi Liang to attack Li province. Deming was then eighteen; he recruited five thousand men, advanced at double speed, kept his orders strict and orderly, and broke the enemy in a single battle. For his merit he was repeatedly promoted to an appointment on the staff of the Prince of Qi, but was dismissed on account of an offense. When the righteous army besieged Chang'an, Prince Yong'an Xiaoji, Prince of Xiangyi Shenfu, Prince of Jiangxia Daozong, and Gaozu's sons-in-law Dou Dan and Zhao Cijing were all imprisoned; the Sui generals Wei Wensheng and Yin Shishi wished to kill them. Deming said to Wensheng: "The guilt is not with these men; killing them would not harm the enemy but would only invite resentment." Wensheng then stopped. When he had an audience with Gaozu, he never spoke of it himself; people at the time praised him as a man of mature character. At the beginning of the Wude era he was appointed Director in the Bureau of Merit. He followed Taizong in attacking Wang Shichong, repeatedly won merit in battle, and was enfeoffed as Baron of Xianwu. At the beginning of the Zhenguan era he served successively as prefect of Chang and Ai provinces. Shortly afterward he died.
7
弟德玄，高宗時為左相。 德玄子懷貞。
His younger brother Dexuan served as Left Chancellor under Gaozong. Dexuan's son was Huai Zhen.
8
懷貞，少有名譽，時兄弟宗族，並以輿馬為事，懷貞獨折節自修，衣服儉素。 聖歷中為清河令，治有能名。 俄歷越州都督、揚州大都督府長史，所在皆以清幹著稱。
Huai Zhen in youth had a fine reputation; at the time his brothers and clansmen all devoted themselves to carriages and horses, but Huai Zhen alone restrained himself and cultivated virtue, dressing plainly and simply. During the Shenglu era he served as magistrate of Qinghe and was known for capable administration. Shortly afterward he served successively as Area Commander of Yue province and Chief Administrator of the Yangzhou Grand Area Command, and everywhere was known for integrity and efficiency.
9
，累遷御史大夫，兼檢校雍州長史。 時韋庶人及安樂公主等干預朝政。 懷貞每諂順委曲取容，改名從一，以避后父之諱，自是名稱日損。 庶人微時乳母王氏，本蠻婢也，特封莒國夫人，嫁為懷貞妻。 俗謂乳母之婿為阿沄，懷貞每因謁見之次及進表疏，列在官位，必曰「皇后阿沄」，時人或以「國沄」呼之，初無慚色。 宦官用權，懷貞尤所畏敬，每視事聽訟，見無須者，誤以接之。 監察御史魏傳弓嘗以內常侍輔信義尤縱暴，將奏劾之。 懷貞曰：「輔常侍深為安樂公主所信任，權勢甚高，言成禍福，何得輒有彈糾？ 」傳弓曰：「今王綱漸壞，君子道消，正由此輩擅權耳！ 若得今日殺之，明日受誅，無所恨。 」懷貞無以答，但固止之。
He was promoted repeatedly to Censor-in-Chief and concurrently Acting Governor of Yongzhou. At that time the Deposed Consort Wei and Princess Anle and others interfered in court affairs. Huai Zhen always fawned and yielded to win favor; he changed his name to Congyi to avoid the taboo on the empress's father's name, and from then on his reputation daily declined. When the Deposed Consort was still obscure, her wet nurse Lady Wang, originally a barbarian slave girl, was specially enfeoffed as Lady of Ju state and given in marriage to Huai Zhen as his wife. Common speech calls a wet nurse's son-in-law an "Ayun"; whenever Huai Zhen had an audience or submitted a memorial listing his official rank, he always wrote "the Empress's Ayun," and people at the time sometimes called him "State Ayun" — yet at first he showed no shame. Eunuchs wielded power, and Huai Zhen feared and honored them above all; whenever he held court and heard cases, if he saw a beardless man he would mistakenly treat him as a eunuch and defer to him. Investigating Censor Wei Chuanggong once intended to memorialize and impeach Palace Attendant Fu Xinyi, who was especially violent and overbearing. Huai Zhen said: "Attendant Fu is deeply trusted by Princess Anle; his power is very great and his words bring fortune or disaster — how can you rashly impeach him?" Chuanggong said: "Today the royal norms are gradually breaking down and the way of the gentleman is fading — it is precisely because men like these monopolize power!" If I can kill him today and be executed tomorrow, I shall have no regret. Huai Zhen had no reply but firmly restrained him.
10
韋庶人敗，左遷濠州司馬。 尋擢授益州大都督府長史。 以附會太平公主，累拜侍中、兼御史大夫，代韋安石為尚書左僕射，監修國史，賜爵魏國公。
When the Deposed Consort Wei fell, he was demoted to Military Advisor of Hao prefecture. Shortly afterward he was promoted and appointed Chief Administrator of the Yizhou Grand Area Command. By currying favor with Princess Taiping he was repeatedly promoted to Palace Attendant and concurrently Censor-in-Chief, replaced Wei Anshi as Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, supervised compilation of the national history, and was granted the title Duke of Wei.
11
睿宗為金仙、玉真二公主創立兩觀，料功甚多，時議皆以為不可。 唯懷貞贊成其事，躬自監役。 懷貞族弟詹事司直維鍌謂懷貞曰：「兄位極臺袞，當思獻可替否，以輔明主。 奈何校量瓦木，廁跡工匠之間，欲令海內何所瞻仰也？ 」懷貞不能對，而監作如故。 時人為之語曰：「竇僕射前為韋氏國沄，後作公主邑丞。 」言懷貞伏事公主，同於邑官也。
Ruizong founded two abbeys for the Princesses Jinxian and Yuzhen; the estimated labor was very great, and opinion at the time held it inadvisable. Only Huai Zhen approved the project and personally supervised the labor. Huai Zhen's clansman and younger cousin Wei Jian, Direct Clerk in the Household of the Heir Apparent, said to Huai Zhen: "Brother, you have reached the highest offices of state; you ought to think of offering approval or rejection to assist the enlightened sovereign." Why instead measure tiles and timber and mingle with the craftsmen — what is there in this for the realm to look up to? Huai Zhen could not reply but continued supervising construction as before. People at the time made a saying about him: "Vice Director Dou was first the Wei clan's State Ayun, and afterward became the princess's district aide." This meant that Huai Zhen served the princess like a district official.
12
，太平公主逆謀事泄，懷貞懼罪，投水而死。 追戮其屍，改姓毒氏。
When Princess Taiping's treasonous plot was exposed, Huai Zhen, fearing punishment, threw himself into the water and died. His corpse was posthumously punished; his surname was changed to Du.
13
德明族弟孝諶。
Deming's clansman and younger cousin was Dou Xiaochen.
14
孝諶，刑部尚書誕之子，昭成順聖皇后父也。 則天時，歷太常少卿、潤州刺史。 ，后母龐氏被酷吏所陷，誣與后咒詛不道，孝諶左遷羅州司馬而卒。
Dou Xiaochen was the son of Minister of Justice Dan and father of Empress Zhaocheng Shunsheng. During the reign of Empress Zetian he served successively as Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and prefect of Run province. The empress's mother Lady Pang was framed by a cruel official, falsely accused of cursing the empress with impiety; Dou Xiaochen was demoted to Military Advisor of Luo prefecture and died.
15
子希瑊、希球、希瓘，並流嶺南。 神龍初，隨例雪免。 景雲年，追贈李諶太尉、邠國公，希瑊襲爵。 玄宗即位，加贈孝諶太保，希瑊等以舅氏，甚見優寵。
His sons Xi Zhang, Xi Qiu, and Xi Guan were all exiled to Lingnan. At the beginning of the Shenlong era they were cleared by precedent. In the Jingyun era Dou Xiaochen was posthumously granted Grand Marshal and Duke of Bin; Xi Zhang inherited the title. When Xuanzong ascended the throne, Dou Xiaochen was further posthumously granted Grand Guardian; Xi Zhang and the others, as maternal uncles of the emperor, received great favor.
16
希瑊累遷太子少傅、豳國公，尋卒。
Xi Zhang was promoted repeatedly to Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent and Duke of Bin, and shortly afterward died.
17
希球官至太子賓客，封冀國公，卒。 及卒，謚曰靖。
Xi Qiu reached the office of Guest of the Heir Apparent, was enfeoffed as Duke of Ji, and died. Upon his death he was given the posthumous title Jing.
18
希瓘初賜爵畢國公，後改名。 初為左散騎常侍，及希球卒，因授開府儀同三司。 玄宗以早失太后，尤重外家，兄弟三人皆國公，食實封。
Xi Guan was first granted the title Duke of Bi state, and later had his name changed. At first he served as Left Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry; when Xi Qiu died, he was accordingly appointed Grand Master of the Palace with the Standing of the Three Excellencies. Because Xuanzong had lost his mother early, he especially valued his maternal kin; all three brothers were made dukes and received actual fiefs.
19
子鍔，又尚玄宗女永昌長公主，恩寵賜賚，實為厚矣。 而兄弟皆貪鄙，過自封植，又甚之。
His son E also married Xuanzong's daughter, Princess Yongchang the Elder; the favor and gifts bestowed were truly generous. Yet the brothers were all greedy and base, going too far in enriching themselves — and in this they went even further.
20
，有竇勉潛交巫祝，勉犯法，坐信其詭說，被停官，放歸田園。 尋以尊老，又授開府儀同三司，依舊朝會。 十三載十二月卒，玄宗哭於行在，贈司徒。 財貨鉅萬。
Dou Mian secretly associated with shamans and diviners; Mian violated the law, and Xi Guan, for believing his deceptive talk, was stripped of office and sent back to his estate. Shortly afterward, on account of his advanced age, he was again granted Grand Master of the Palace with the Standing of the Three Excellencies and continued to attend court as before. In the twelfth month of the thirteenth year he died; Xuanzong wept at the temporary palace and posthumously granted him Minister of Education. His wealth amounted to tens of thousands.
21
從父弟維鍌，好學，以撰著為業。 時宗族咸以外戚，崇飾輿馬，維鍌獨清儉自守。 中書令張說、黃門侍郎盧藏用、給事中裴子餘皆與之親善。 官至水部郎中卒。 撰《吉凶禮要》二十卷，行於代。
His younger cousin of the same grandfather, Wei Jian, loved learning and made authorship his occupation. At the time the whole clan, as maternal kin, gloried in carriages and horses, but Wei Jian alone maintained himself in plain frugality. Chief Minister of the Secretariat Zhang Yue, Vice Director of the Chancellery Lu Zangyong, and Supervising Secretary Pei Ziyu were all on close terms with him. He reached the office of Director in the Bureau of Waterways and died. He compiled twenty juan of Essentials of Auspicious and Inauspicious Rites, which circulated in his age.
22
=長孫敞=
Zhangsun Chang
23
長孫敞，文德順聖皇后之叔父也。 仕隋為左衛郎將。 煬帝幸江都，留敞守京城禁苑。 及義旗入關，率子弟迎謁於新豐，從平京城，以功除將作少監。 出為杞州刺史。 貞觀初，坐贓免。 太宗以后親，常令內給絹以供私費。 尋拜宗正少卿，致仕加金紫光祿大夫，累封平原郡公。 卒，贈幽州都督，謚曰良，陪葬昭陵。 從父弟操敞從父弟操，周大司徒、薛國公覽之子也。 武德中，為陜東道行臺金部郎中，出為陜州刺史。 自州東引水入城，以代井汲，百姓於今利之。 貞觀中，歷洺州刺史、益揚二州都督府長史，並有善政。 二十三年，以子詮尚太宗女新城公主，拜岐州刺史。 永徽初，加金紫光祿大夫，賜爵樂壽男。 尋卒，贈吏部尚書、并州都督，謚曰安。
Zhangsun Chang was the uncle of Empress Wende Shunsheng. He served the Sui as Commandant of the Left Guard. When Emperor Yang visited Jiangdu, he left Chang to guard the imperial park of the capital. When the righteous banner entered the Pass, he led his sons and younger kinsmen to welcome and pay respects at Xinfeng; he followed in pacifying the capital and for his merit was appointed Vice Director of the Directorate of Palace Buildings. He was sent out as prefect of Qi province. At the beginning of the Zhenguan era he was dismissed on account of corruption. Because he was the empress's kin, Taizong regularly had silk supplied from within the palace for his private expenses. Shortly afterward he was appointed Vice Director of the Court of the Imperial Clan; upon retirement he was given the title Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon, and was repeatedly enfeoffed as Duke of Pingyuan commandery. He died; he was posthumously granted Area Commander of You province, given the posthumous title Liang, and buried with honor at Zhaoling. Chang's younger cousin of the same grandfather, Cao, was the son of Zhou Grand Minister of Education, Duke of Xue Lan. During the Wude era he served as Director in the Bureau of Revenue on the Eastern Shaanxi Circuit Executive, then was sent out as prefect of Shan province. He led water from east of the prefectural seat into the city to replace well-drawn water; the people benefit from this to this day. During the Zhenguan era he served successively as prefect of Ming province and Chief Administrator of the Grand Area Commands of Yi and Yang provinces, and everywhere had good administration. In the twenty-third year, because his son Quan married Taizong's daughter Princess Xincheng, he was appointed prefect of Qi province. At the beginning of the Yonghui era he was given the title Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon and granted the title Baron of Leshou. Shortly afterward he died; he was posthumously granted Minister of the Civil Service and Area Commander of Bing province, and given the posthumous title An.
24
詮官至尚書奉御。 詮即侍中韓瑗妻弟也。 及瑗得罪，事連於詮，減死配流巂州。 詮至流所，縣令希旨杖殺之。 趙持滿詮之甥有趙持滿者，工書善射，力搏猛獸，捷及奔馬； 而親仁愛眾，多所交結，京師無貴賤皆愛慕之。 初為涼州長史，嘗逐野馬，自後射之，無不洞於胸腋，邊人深伏之。 許敬宗懼其作難，誣與詮及無忌同反。 及拷訊，終無異詞，且曰：「身可殺，辭不可奪。 」吏竟代為款以殺之。
Quan reached the office of Palace Attendant of the Imperial Household. Quan was the younger brother-in-law of Palace Attendant Han Yuan. When Yuan was punished, the affair implicated Quan; his death sentence was commuted and he was exiled to Xi prefecture. When Quan reached his place of exile, the magistrate, seeking to please his superiors, had him beaten to death. Quan's nephew Zhao Chiman was skilled at calligraphy and archery, could wrestle fierce beasts by strength, and was as swift as a running horse. Moreover he was affectionate and benevolent toward the multitude and had many connections; in the capital none, high or low, failed to admire him. At first he served as Chief Administrator of Liang province; he once chased wild horses and shot them from behind — none failed to be pierced through chest or flank — and the frontier people deeply admired him. Xu Jingzong feared he would raise trouble and falsely accused him of conspiring with Quan and Wuji to rebel. Under torture he never changed his words and said: "My person may be killed, but my testimony cannot be taken away." The officials finally forged a confession on his behalf and killed him.
25
=武承嗣=
Wu Chengsi
26
武承嗣，荊州都督士矱之孫，則天順聖皇后兄子也。 初，士矱娶相里氏，生元慶、元爽。 又娶楊氏，生三女：長適越王府功曹賀蘭越石，次則天，次適郭氏。 士矱卒後，兄子惟良、懷運及元爽等遇楊氏失禮。 及則天立為皇后，追贈士矱為司徒、周忠孝王，封楊氏代國夫人。 賀蘭越石早卒，封其妻為韓國夫人。 尋又加贈士矱為太尉，楊氏改封為榮國夫人。 時元慶仕為宗正少卿，元爽為少府少監，惟良為衛尉少卿。 榮國夫人恨其疇日薄己，諷皇后抗疏請出元慶等為外職，佯為退讓，其實惡之也。 於是元慶為龍州刺史，元爽為濠州刺史，惟良為始州刺史。 元慶至州病卒，元爽自濠州又配流振州而死。
Wu Chengsi was the grandson of Area Commander of Jing province Shiyue and the nephew of Empress Zetian Shunsheng. At first Shiyue married Lady Xiangli and had Yuanqing and Yuanshuang. He then married Lady Yang and had three daughters: the eldest married Helan Yueshi, Functionary of the Prince of Yue's household; the second was Zetian; the third married into the Guo clan. After Shiyue died, his brother's sons Weiliang and Huaiyun and Yuanshuang and the others treated Lady Yang with disrespect. When Zetian was established as empress, Shiyue was posthumously granted Minister of Education and the title Loyal and Filial King of Zhou; Lady Yang was enfeoffed as Lady of Dai state. Helan Yueshi died early; his wife was enfeoffed as Lady of Han state. Shortly afterward Shiyue was further posthumously granted Grand Marshal; Lady Yang's title was changed to Lady of Rong state. At the time Yuanqing served as Vice Director of the Court of the Imperial Clan, Yuanshuang as Vice Director of the Court of the Imperial Manufactories, and Weiliang as Vice Director of the Court of the Imperial Guard. Lady Rong resented their past slighting of her and prompted the empress to submit a memorial requesting that Yuanqing and the others be sent to outside posts, feigning modesty while in fact hating them. Thereupon Yuanqing was made prefect of Long province, Yuanshuang prefect of Hao province, and Weiliang prefect of Shi province. Yuanqing reached his prefecture and died of illness; Yuanshuang was again exiled from Hao province to Zhen province and died there.
27
乾封年，惟良與弟淄州刺史懷運，以嶽牧例集於泰山之下。 時韓國夫人女賀蘭氏在宮中，頗承恩寵。 則天意欲除之，諷高宗幸其母宅，因惟良等獻食，則天密令人以毒藥貯賀蘭氏食中，賀蘭氏食之，暴卒，歸罪於惟良、懷運，乃誅之。 仍諷百僚抗表請改其姓為蝮氏，絕其屬籍。 元爽等緣坐配流嶺外而死，乃以韓國夫人之子敏之為士矱嗣，改姓武氏，累拜左侍極、蘭臺太史，襲爵周國公。 仍令鳩集學士李嗣真、吳兢之徒，於蘭臺刊正經史，並著撰傳記。
In the Qianfeng era Weiliang and his younger brother Huaiyun, prefect of Zi province, assembled at the foot of Mount Tai according to the custom for mountain-sacrificing prefects. At the time Lady Helan, daughter of Lady Han, was in the palace and enjoyed considerable favor. Zetian wished to eliminate them; she prompted Gaozong to visit their mother's residence, and when Weiliang and the others presented food, Zetian secretly had someone place poison in Lady Helan's food; Lady Helan ate it and died suddenly, and the blame was placed on Weiliang and Huaiyun, who were then executed. She further prompted the hundred officials to submit memorials requesting that their surname be changed to Fu and their clan registers severed. Yuanshuang and the others, implicated by association, were exiled beyond the Ling range and died; then Minzhi, son of Lady Han, was made Shiyue's heir, his surname was changed to Wu, he was repeatedly promoted to Left Attending Grand Secretary and Grand Astrologer of the Orchid Terrace, and inherited the title Duke of Zhou. He was further ordered to gather scholars such as Li Sizhen and Wu Jing at the Orchid Terrace to revise the classics and histories and also compose biographical works.
28
敏之既年少色美，烝於榮國夫人，恃寵多愆犯，則天頗不悅之。 ，榮國夫人卒，則天出內大瑞錦，令敏之造佛像追福，敏之自隱用之。 又司衛少卿楊思儉女有殊色，高宗及則天自選以為太子妃，成有定日矣，敏之又逼而淫焉。 及在榮國服內，私釋衰绖，著吉服，奏妓樂。 時太平公主尚幼，往來榮國之家，宮人侍行，又嘗為敏之所逼。 俄而奸汙事發，配流雷州，行至韶州，以馬韁自縊而死。
Minzhi was young and handsome and had illicit relations with Lady Rong; relying on favor he committed many offenses, and Zetian was quite displeased with him. When Lady Rong died, Zetian brought out great auspicious brocade from within the palace and ordered Minzhi to make Buddhist images for merit on her behalf; Minzhi secretly kept it for himself. Moreover the daughter of Vice Director of the Court of the Imperial Guard Yang Sijian was of exceptional beauty; Gaozong and Zetian personally selected her as crown princess and a date had been set, yet Minzhi forced himself upon her and violated her. While in mourning for Lady Rong he privately cast off his hemp mourning garments, put on festive dress, and had singing girls perform. At the time Princess Taiping was still young and visited Lady Rong's household; palace women accompanied her, and she too was once forced by Minzhi. Shortly afterward his licentious crimes were exposed; he was exiled to Lei province, and en route at Shao province he hanged himself with a horse bridle.
29
承嗣，元爽子也。 敏之死後，自嶺南召還，拜尚衣奉御，襲祖爵周國公。 俄遷秘書監。 則天臨朝，追尊士矱為忠孝太皇，置崇先府官屬，五代祖已下，皆為王。 嗣聖元年，以承嗣為禮部尚書。 尋除太常卿、同中書門下三品。 垂拱中，轉春官尚書，依舊知政事。 ，代蘇良嗣為文昌左相、同鳳閣鸞臺三品，兼知內史事。
Chengsi was Yuanshuang's son. After Minzhi's death he was recalled from Lingnan, appointed Palace Attendant of the Imperial Wardrobe, and inherited his grandfather's title Duke of Zhou. Shortly afterward he was transferred to Director of the Palace Library. When Zetian presided over court, Shiyue was posthumously honored as the Loyal and Filial Grand Emperor; the Chongxian Office and its staff were established, and from the fifth-generation ancestor downward all were made kings. In the first year of Sisheng, Chengsi was made Minister of Rites. Shortly afterward he was appointed Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and given the status of Associate Chief Minister of the Secretariat and Chancellery of the Third Rank. During the Chuigong era he was transferred to Minister of the Spring Office and continued as before to manage state affairs. He replaced Su Liangsi as Left Chancellor of Wenchang, Associate of the Third Rank of the Phoenix Pavilion and Orchid Terrace, and concurrently managed Secretariat affairs.
30
，於東都創置武氏七廟，追尊周文王為始祖文皇帝，王子武為睿祖康皇帝，云武氏之先也。 后五代祖贈太原靖王居常為嚴祖成皇帝，高祖贈趙肅恭王克己為肅祖章敬皇帝，曾祖贈魏康王儉為烈祖昭安皇帝，祖贈周安成王華為顯祖文穆皇帝，考忠孝太皇為太祖孝明高皇帝，妣皆隨帝號曰皇后。 元慶為梁憲王，元爽為魏德王。 又追封伯父及兄弟俱為王，諸姑姊為長公主。 於是封承嗣為魏王，元慶子夏官尚書三思為梁王，后從父兄子納言攸寧為建昌王，太子通事舍人攸歸為九江王，司禮卿重規為高平王，左衛親府中郎將載德為潁川王，右衛將軍攸暨為千乘王，司農卿懿宗為河內王，左千牛中郎將嗣宗為臨川王，右衛勛二府中郎將攸宜為建安王，尚乘直長攸望為會稽王，太子通事舍人攸緒為安平王，攸止為恆安王。 又封承嗣男延基為南陽王，延秀為淮陽王，三思男崇訓為高陽王，崇烈為新安王，后兄子贈陳王承業男延暉為嗣陳王，延祚為咸安王。
At the Eastern Capital he newly established the seven ancestral temples of the Wu clan, posthumously honoring King Wen of Zhou as Founding Ancestor Emperor Wen and Prince Wu as Sagacious Ancestor Emperor Kang, declaring them the forebears of the Wu clan. The empress's fifth-generation ancestor, posthumously granted King Jing of Taiyuan Juchang, was honored as Stern Ancestor Emperor Cheng; great-great-grandfather, posthumously granted King Su Gong of Zhao Keji, as Solemn Ancestor Emperor Zhang Jing; great-grandfather, posthumously granted King Kang of Wei Jian, as Majestic Ancestor Emperor Zhao An; grandfather, posthumously granted King Ancheng of Zhou Hua, as Illustrious Ancestor Emperor Wen Mu; father the Loyal and Filial Grand Emperor as Grand Ancestor Emperor Xiao Ming Gao — their consorts all followed the imperial titles as empresses. Yuanqing was made King Xian of Liang, Yuanshuang King De of Wei. Paternal uncles and brothers were all posthumously enfeoffed as kings, and aunts and elder sisters as elder princesses. Thereupon Chengsi was enfeoffed as King of Wei; Yuanqing's son, Minister of the Summer Office Sansi, as King of Liang; the empress's elder male cousin's son, Remonstrating Secretary Youning, as King of Jianchang; Crown Prince's Communication Attendant Yougui as King of Jiujiang; Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Chonggui as King of Gaoping; Commandant of the Left Guard Personal Guard Zhonglang Jiang Zaide as King of Yingchuan; General of the Right Guard Youji as King of Qiansheng; Director of the Court of Imperial Granaries Yizong as King of Henei; Commandant of the Left Thousand-Ox Zhonglang Jiang Sizong as King of Linchuan; Commandant of the Right Guard Merit Second Office Zhonglang Jiang Youyi as King of Jian'an; Direct Attendant of the Imperial Carriage Youwang as King of Kuaiji; Crown Prince's Communication Attendant Youxu as King of Ping'an; and Youzhi as King of Heng'an. Chengsi's sons Yanji and Yanxiu were enfeoffed as King of Nanyang and King of Huaiyang; Sansi's sons Chongxun and Chonglie as King of Gaoyang and King of Xin'an; the empress's elder brother's posthumously granted son, King of Chen Chengye's son Yanhui as Heir King of Chen, and Yanzuo as King of Xian'an.
31
承嗣嘗諷則天革命，盡誅皇室諸王及公卿中不附己者，承嗣從父弟三思又盛贊其計，天下於今冤之。 俄又賜承嗣實封千戶，仍監修國史。 承嗣自為次當為皇儲，令鳳閣舍人張嘉福諷諭百姓抗表陳請，則天竟不許。 ，授特進。 尋拜太子太保，罷知政事。 承嗣以不得立為皇太子，怏怏而卒，贈太尉、并州牧，謚曰宣。
Chengsi once urged Zetian to change the dynasty and execute all the imperial princes and high officials who did not support him; Chengsi's younger cousin of the same grandfather Sansi also strongly praised the plan — the realm still resents this. Shortly afterward Chengsi was granted an actual fief of one thousand households and continued to supervise compilation of the national history. Chengsi considered himself next in line to be crown prince and had Phoenix Pavilion Drafter Zhang Jiafu prompt the common people to submit memorials requesting it, but Zetian would not consent. He was granted Special Advancement. Shortly afterward he was appointed Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent and removed from managing state affairs. Because Chengsi was not established as crown prince, he died discontented; he was posthumously granted Grand Marshal and Governor of Bing province, with the posthumous title Xuan.
32
子延基襲爵，則天避其父名，封為繼魏王。 尋與其妻永泰郡主及懿德太子等，話及張易之兄弟出入宮中，恐有不利，後忿爭不協，泄之，則天聞而大怒，咸令自殺。 復以承嗣次子延義為繼魏王。
His son Yanji inherited the title; Zetian avoided his father's name and enfeoffed him as Heir King of Wei. Shortly afterward he, his wife the Princess of Yongtai commandery, Crown Prince Yide, and others discussed the Zhang Yizhi brothers' coming and going within the palace and feared harm; afterward, in angry disagreement, the matter was leaked; Zetian heard and was greatly enraged and ordered them all to kill themselves. Chengsi's second son Yanyi was again made Heir King of Wei.
33
中宗即位，侍中敬暉等以唐室中興，武氏諸王宜削其王爵，乃率群官上表曰：
When Zhongzong ascended the throne, Palace Attendant Jing Hui and others, holding that the Tang house had been restored, argued that the Wu princes should be stripped of their royal titles; they therefore led the officials in submitting a memorial saying:
34
中書舍人岑義之詞也。 上答曰：
This was the wording of Secretariat Drafter Cen Yi. The emperor replied:
35
於是降封梁王三思為德靜郡王，量減實封二百戶，定王、駙馬都尉攸暨為樂壽郡王，河內郡王懿宗為耿國公，建昌郡王攸寧為江國公，會稽郡王攸望為鄴國公，臨川郡王嗣宗為管國公，建安郡王攸宜為息國公，高平郡王重規為鄶國公，繼魏王延義為魏國公，安平郡王攸緒為巢國公，高陽郡王、駙馬都尉崇訓為酆國公，淮陽郡王延秀為桓國公，咸安郡王延祚為咸安郡公。
Thereupon King of Liang Sansi was demoted to Prince of Dejing commandery with a reduction of two hundred households from his actual fief; King Ding, Commandant of the Horse Guards Youji, to Prince of Leshou commandery; Prince of Henei commandery Yizong to Duke of Geng state; Prince of Jianchang commandery Youning to Duke of Jiang state; Prince of Kuaiji commandery Youwang to Duke of Ye state; Prince of Linchuan commandery Sizong to Duke of Guan state; Prince of Jian'an commandery Youyi to Duke of Xi state; Prince of Gaoping commandery Chonggui to Duke of Kuai state; Heir King of Wei Yanyi to Duke of Wei state; Prince of Ping'an commandery Youxu to Duke of Chao state; Prince of Gaoyang commandery, Commandant of the Horse Guards Chongxun to Duke of Feng state; Prince of Huaiyang commandery Yanxiu to Duke of Huan state; and Prince of Xian'an commandery Yanzuo to Duke of Xian'an commandery.
36
中宗時，嗣宗至曹州刺史，攸宜工部尚書，重規岐州刺史，相次病卒。 攸望至太常卿，左遷春州司馬而死。 延秀伏誅後，武氏宗屬緣坐誅死及配流，殆將盡矣。 ，制削士彟帝號，依舊追贈太原王，妻楊氏亦削后號，依舊為太原王妃。 承嗣子延秀延秀，承嗣第二子也。 則天時，突厥默啜上言有女請和親，制延秀與閻知微俱往突厥，將親迎默啜女為妻。 既而默啜執知微，入冠趙、定等州，故延秀久不得還。 神龍初，默啜更請通和，先令延秀送款，始得歸，封桓國公，又授左衛中郎將。 時武崇訓為安樂公主婿，即延秀從父兄，數引至主第。 延秀久在蕃中，解突厥語，常於主第，延秀唱突厥歌，作胡旋舞，有姿媚，主甚喜之。 及崇訓死，延秀得幸，遂尚公主。
During Zhongzong's reign Sizong reached prefect of Cao province, Youyi Minister of Works, and Chonggui prefect of Qi province; they died of illness one after another. Youwang reached Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, was demoted to Military Advisor of Chun prefecture, and died. After Yanxiu was executed, Wu clansmen implicated by association were executed or exiled until nearly all were gone. An edict stripped Shiyue of his imperial title and restored the posthumous grant of King of Taiyuan; his wife Lady Yang likewise lost her empress title and was restored as Princess of Taiyuan. Chengsi's son Yanxiu was Chengsi's second son. During Zetian's reign the Türk Mo-ch'o reported that he had a daughter and requested a marriage alliance; Yanxiu was ordered to go with Yan Zhiwei to the Türks to personally welcome Mo-ch'o's daughter as his wife. Shortly afterward Mo-ch'o seized Zhiwei and invaded Zhao, Ding, and other prefectures, so Yanxiu was long unable to return. At the beginning of the Shenlong era Mo-ch'o again requested peace; he first had Yanxiu send pledges of submission, and only then was Yanxiu able to return; he was enfeoffed as Duke of Huan state and further appointed Commandant of the Left Guard. At that time Wu Chongxun, Princess Anle's husband and Yanxiu's older male cousin on their shared grandfather's side, repeatedly brought Yanxiu to the princess's residence. Yanxiu had spent many years among the barbarians and knew Türk; at the princess's residence he often sang Türk songs and danced the whirling Hu-xuan dance. Graceful and alluring, he pleased the princess greatly. After Chongxun died, Yanxiu won her favor and married the princess.
37
主，韋后所生男女中最小。 初，中宗遷於房州，欲達州境，生於路次。 性惠敏，容質秀絕。 中宗、韋后愛龐日深，恣其所欲，奏請無不允許。 恃寵橫縱，權傾天下，自王侯宰相已下，除拜多出其門。 所營第宅並造安樂佛寺，擬於宮掖，巧妙過之。 令楊務廉於城西造定昆池於其莊，延袤數里。 出降之時，以皇后仗發於宮中，中宗與韋后御安福門觀之，燈燭供擬，徹明如晝。 延秀拜度日，授太常卿，兼右衛將軍、駙馬都尉，改封恆國公，實封五百戶。 廢休祥宅，於金城坊造宅，窮極壯麗，帑藏為之空竭。 崇訓子數歲，因加金紫光祿大夫、太常卿同正員、左衛將軍，封鎬國公，賜實封五百戶，以嗣其父。 公主產男滿月，中宗、韋后幸其第，就第放赦，遣宰臣李嶠、文士宋之問、沈佺期、張說、閻朝隱等數百人賦詩美之。
The princess was the youngest of the sons and daughters Empress Wei had borne. When Zhongzong was first sent into exile at Fangzhou and had not yet reached the prefecture, she was born on the road. Quick-witted by nature, she was also of surpassing beauty. Zhongzong and Empress Wei grew more indulgent toward her every day, granting her every wish without exception. Secure in imperial favor, she acted with arrogant impunity; her power overshadowed the realm, and from kings and chancellors down, most appointments came through her household. The mansions she built and the Anle Buddhist Temple she founded were modeled on the palace itself—and surpassed it in elegance. She had Yang Wulian construct the Dingkun Pool at her estate west of the city, a body of water several li across. When she went forth to marry, the empress's honor guard departed from within the palace; Zhongzong and Empress Wei took their places at Anfu Gate to watch. Lamps and candles were set out in such abundance that the night shone bright as day. A few days after Yanxiu completed the marriage obeisances, he was made Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, concurrently General of the Right Guard and Commandant of the Horse Guards; his title was changed to Duke of Heng with an actual fief of five hundred households. They tore down the Xiuxiang residence and built a new mansion in Jincheng Ward, lavish beyond measure, draining the treasury dry. Chongxun's son, only a few years old, was made Supervising Imperial Secretary with the Golden-purple Floppy, Regular-ranked Minister of Ceremonies, and General of the Left Guard; he was enfeoffed as Duke of Hao with five hundred actual fief households to succeed his father. When the princess's newborn son completed his first month, Zhongzong and Empress Wei visited her residence and proclaimed an amnesty on the spot. They dispatched several hundred court ministers and literati—including Li Qiao, Song Zhiwen, Shen Quanqi, Zhang Yue, and Yan Chaoyin—to compose poems in celebration.
38
延秀既恃恩，放縱無所忌憚。 又公主府倉曹符鳳知延秀有不臣之心，遂說曰：「今天下蒼生，猶以武氏為念，大周必可再興。 按讖書云『黑衣神孫披天裳』，駙馬即神皇之孫也。 」每勸令著皁襖子以應之。 及韋庶人敗，延秀與公主在內宅，格戰良久。 皆斬之。 後追貶為悖逆庶人。 元慶子三思三思，元慶子也。 少以后族累轉右衛將軍。 則天臨朝，擢拜夏官尚書。 及革命，封梁王，賜實封一千戶。 尋拜天官尚書。 ，轉春官尚書，監修國史。 ，檢校內史。 二年，進拜特進、太子賓客，仍並依舊監修國史。
Yanxiu, emboldened by imperial favor, gave himself over to reckless excess without restraint. The princess's household warehouse clerk Fufeng, perceiving Yanxiu's disloyal ambitions, urged him: "The people of the realm still look to the House of Wu—the Great Zhou can surely rise again. Prophecy books say, 'The divine grandson in black robes spreads heaven's garment'—and you, the imperial son-in-law, are the divine empress's grandson. " He repeatedly urged Yanxiu to wear black jackets to fulfill the prophecy. When the Deposed Consort Wei fell, Yanxiu and the princess barricaded themselves in the inner quarters and fought hand to hand for a long while. Both were beheaded. She was later posthumously stripped of rank and demoted to Commoner of Rebellion and Treason. Yuanqing's son Sansi was Yuanqing's son. In his youth he rose through the empress's kinship network, eventually becoming General of the Right Guard. When Zetian assumed the regency, he was promoted to Minister of the Summer Office. When she declared the new dynasty, he was enfeoffed as King of Liang with an actual fief of one thousand households. Shortly afterward he was appointed Minister of the Personnel Office. He was transferred to Minister of the Office of Rites and placed in charge of compiling the national history. He was also made Acting Imperial Secretary. In the second year he was promoted to Special Advancement and Companion to the Heir Apparent, while continuing to oversee compilation of the national history as before.

三思略涉文史，性傾巧便僻，善事人，由是特蒙信任。 則天數幸其第，賞賜甚厚。 時薛懷義、張易之、昌宗皆承恩顧。 三思與承嗣每折節事之。 懷義欲乘馬，承嗣、三思必為之執轡。 又贈昌宗詩，盛稱昌宗才貌是王子晉後身，仍令朝士遞相屬和。 三思又以則天厭居深宮，又欲與張易之、昌宗等扈從馳騁，以弄其權。 乃請創造三陽宮於嵩高山，興泰宮於萬壽山，請則天每歲臨幸，前後工役甚眾，百姓怨之。
Sansi had some literary and historical learning; crafty and ingratiating by nature, he excelled at winning people over and thereby earned Zetian's special trust. Zetian often visited his home, lavishing rich rewards upon him. At the time Xue Huaiyi, Zhang Yizhi, and Changzong all enjoyed the empress's favor. Sansi and Chengsi humiliated themselves in serving them. Whenever Huaiyi wanted to mount a horse, Chengsi and Sansi would hold the reins for him. He also wrote Changzong a poem extravagantly praising his talent and looks as the reincarnation of Prince Zijin, and had court officials compose matching verses in turn. Sansi also knew that Zetian was weary of the deep palace; he wanted to ride and hunt at her side with Zhang Yizhi, Changzong, and the rest, thereby to play with power in the open. He therefore petitioned to build Sanyang Palace on Mount Song and Xingtai Palace on Mount Wanshou, asking that Zetian visit each year. The labor levies were enormous, and the people groaned under them.

神龍初，進拜司空、同中書門下三品，加實封五百戶，固辭不受。 未幾，隨例降封為德靜郡王，量減實封二百戶。 尋拜左散騎常侍，則天遺制令復其所減實封。
At the beginning of the Shenlong era he was promoted to Minister of Works and concurrent Third Rank at the Secretariat-Chancellery, with five hundred additional actual fief households, but he firmly declined. Before long, following the usual precedent, he was demoted to Prince of Dejing commandery, with two hundred households cut from his actual fief. Shortly afterward he was appointed Left Regular Attendant of Cavalry; Zetian's posthumous edict restored the households that had been taken from his fief.

初，敬暉等立功後，掌知國政，三思慮其更為己患，而令其子崇訓因安樂公主構誣敬暉等，並流於嶺表而死。 自是三思威權日盛，軍國政事，多所參綜。 敬暉等所斥黜者，皆能引復舊職，令百官復修則天之法。 時人皆言其陰懷篡逆，以比曹孟德、司馬仲達。
After Jing Hui and his allies had seized power through their coup, Sansi feared they would threaten him again. Through Princess Anle he had his son Chongxun fabricate charges against Jing Hui and the others; all were exiled beyond the Ling Mountains and died there. From then on Sansi's power grew daily, and he meddled extensively in military and civil affairs. Officials whom Jing Hui and his faction had dismissed, he restored to office; he ordered the bureaucracy to resume Zetian's policies. People at the time whispered that he secretly harbored usurpation, comparing him to Cao Cao and Sima Yi.

雍州人韋月將、高軫等並上疏言三思父子必為逆亂。 三思知而求索其罪。 有司希旨，奏：「月將坐當棄市，軫配流嶺外」。 黃門侍郎宋璟執奏云：「月將所犯，不合至死。 」三思怒，竟斥宋璟為外職。 三思既猜嫉正士，嘗言「不知何等名作好人，唯有向我好者，是好人耳。 」又與其所親兵部尚書宗楚客、將作大匠宗晉卿、太府卿紀處訥、鴻臚卿甘元柬遞相引致，幹黷時政。 侍御史周利用、冉祖雍，太僕丞李悛，光祿丞宋之遜，監察御史姚紹之等五人，常為其耳目，時人呼為「三思五狗」。
Wei Yuejiang of Yongzhou, Gao Zhen, and others submitted memorials warning that Sansi and his son would surely rebel. Sansi learned of this and set about finding crimes with which to charge them. The responsible officials, reading his wishes, reported: "Yuejiang's crime warrants execution by decapitation and display; Zhen is to be exiled beyond the Ling Mountains." Vice Director of the Yellow Gate Song Jing objected in a formal memorial: "Yuejiang's offense does not merit death. " Enraged, Sansi had Song Jing banished to an outer post. Suspicious and hostile toward upright men, Sansi once said: "I don't know what makes a good man—only those who are good to me are good men. " He also colluded with his cronies—Minister of War Zong Chuke, Grand Master of Works Zong Jinqing, Director of the Court of the Imperial Treasury Ji Chunna, and Director of the Court of State Ceremonial Gan Yuanjian—each pulling the others into power and corrupting the governance of the day. Supervising Censor Zhou Liyong, Ran Zuyong, Deputy Director of the Court of the Imperial Stud Li Quan, Deputy Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments Song Zhixun, and Investigating Censor Yao Shaozhi—these five served as his eyes and ears; people called them "Sansi's Five Dogs."

中宗尋又制：武氏崇恩廟，一依天授時舊禮享祭，其吳陵、順陵，並置官員，皆三思意也。
Zhongzong soon issued an edict: the Wu clan's Temple of Honored Grace was to be maintained with sacrifices according to the old Tianshou rites; officials were appointed for Wu Ling and Shun Ling—all at Sansi's instigation.

三思既與韋庶人及上官昭容私通，嘗忌節湣太子，又因安樂公主密謀廢黜之。 三年七月，太子率羽林大將軍李多祚等，發左右羽林兵，殺三思及其子崇訓於其第，並殺其親黨十餘人。 俄而事變，太子既死，中宗為三思舉哀，廢朝五日，贈太尉，追封梁王，謚曰宣。 安樂公主又以節湣太子首致祭於三思及崇訓靈柩前。 睿宗踐祚，以三思父子俱有逆節，制令斫棺暴屍，平其墳墓。 三思子崇訓崇訓，三思第二子也。 則天時，封為高陽郡王。 長安中，尚安樂郡主。 時三思用事於朝，欲寵其禮。 中宗為太子在東宮，三思宅在天津橋南，自重光門內行親迎禮，歸於其宅。 三思又令宰臣李嶠、蘇味道，詞人沈佺期、宋之問、徐彥伯、張說、閻朝隱、崔融、崔湜、鄭愔等賦《花燭行》以美之。 其時張易之、昌宗、宗楚客兄弟貴盛，時假詞於人，皆有新句。 崇訓授左衛中郎將。 神龍元年，拜駙馬都尉，遷太常卿，兼左衛將軍。 降封酆國公，仍賜實封五百戶，尋徙封鎬國公。 二年，兼太子賓客，攝左衛將軍。 及為節湣太子所殺，優制贈開府儀同三司，追贈魯王，謚曰忠。 從祖弟懿宗懿宗，則天伯父士逸之孫也。 父元忠，高宗時仕至倉部郎中。 天授年，封士逸為蜀王，懿宗封為河內郡王，歷遷洛州長史、左金吾衛大將軍。 萬歲通天年中，契丹賊帥孫萬榮寇河北，命懿宗為大總管討之。 軍次趙州，用聞賊將至冀州，懿宗懼，便欲棄軍而遁。 人或謂曰：「賊眾極多，然其軍無輜重，以抄掠為資，若按兵以守，勢必離散，因而擊之。 可有大功也。 」懿宗不聽，遂退據相州，時人嗤其怯懦。 由是賊眾進屠趙州而去。 尋又令懿宗安撫河北諸州。
Sansi, who was secretly involved with the Deposed Consort Wei and Shangguan Zhaorong, had long resented Crown Prince Jiemin; through Princess Anle he also plotted to have the crown prince deposed. In the seventh month of the third year the crown prince, leading General of the Feathered Forest Li Duozuo and others, mobilized the Left and Right Feathered Forest armies and killed Sansi and his son Chongxun at their residence, along with more than ten of their close associates. Events soon turned: the crown prince was killed, and Zhongzong held mourning rites for Sansi, suspending court for five days. Sansi was posthumously granted Grand Marshal, re-enfeoffed as King of Liang, and given the posthumous name Xuan. Princess Anle further placed Crown Prince Jiemin's severed head as an offering before the coffins of Sansi and Chongxun. When Ruizong took the throne, an edict declared that Sansi and his son had both committed treason; their coffins were broken open, their corpses exposed, and their tombs leveled. Sansi's son Chongxun was Sansi's second son. During Zetian's reign he was enfeoffed as Prince of Gaoyang. During the Chang'an era he married the Lady of Anle. Sansi then dominated the court and wished to magnify the wedding ceremony. Zhongzong was still crown prince in the Eastern Palace; Sansi's house stood south of Tianjin Bridge. The bridegroom's welcoming ceremony was conducted from within Chongguang Gate, and the bride was escorted to his residence. Sansi further commissioned chancellors Li Qiao and Su Weidao and poets including Shen Quanqi, Song Zhiwen, Xu Yanbo, Zhang Yue, Yan Chaoyin, Cui Rong, Cui Ti, and Zheng Yin to compose "Song of the Flower Candle" in praise of the wedding. At that time Zhang Yizhi, Changzong, and the Zong Chuke brothers were at the height of power and prestige; they often borrowed others' lines, yet each contributed new verses of his own. Chongxun was appointed Commandant of the Left Guard. In the first year of Shenlong he was made Commandant of the Horse Guards, then transferred to Grand Master of Splendid Happiness while concurrently serving as General of the Left Guard. He was demoted to Duke of Feng but retained five hundred actual fief households; shortly afterward his title was changed to Duke of Hao. In the second year he was made concurrent Companion to the Heir Apparent, acting as General of the Left Guard. After Crown Prince Jiemin killed him, a special edict posthumously granted him Honorary Grand General with the Presidency of the Department of State Affairs, enfeoffed him as King of Lu, and gave him the posthumous name Zhong. Yizong, a younger male cousin on the shared grandfather's side, was the grandson of Zetian's paternal uncle Shiyi. His father Yuanzhong rose during Gaozong's reign to Bureau Director in the Ministry of Revenue. In the Tianshou era Shiyi was enfeoffed as King of Shu and Yizong as Prince of Henei; Yizong later served as Long-term Administrator of Luozhou and General of the Left Golden Crow Guard. In the Wansui Tongtian era the Khitan rebel leader Sun Wanrong invaded Hebei; Yizong was appointed Grand Commander to suppress him. When the army reached Zhaozhou and word came that the rebels were about to reach Jizhou, Yizong panicked and wanted to abandon his troops and flee. Someone advised him: "The rebel force is very large, but they have no baggage train and live by plunder. If you hold your ground, they will inevitably scatter—and then you can strike. You can win great merit. " Yizong refused to listen. He withdrew to Xiangzhou, and people mocked him for his cowardice. The rebels then advanced, massacred Zhaozhou, and moved on. Shortly afterward Yizong was again ordered to pacify the prefectures of Hebei.

先是，百姓有脅從賊眾，後得歸來者。 懿宗以為同反，總殺之。 仍生刳取其膽，後行刑，流血盈前，言笑自若。 初。 孫萬榮別帥何阿小攻陷冀州，亦多屠害士女。 至是，時人號懿宗與阿小為兩何，為之語曰：「唯此兩何，殺人最多。 」懿宗又自天授已來，嘗受中旨，推鞫制獄，王公大臣，多被陷成其罪，時人以為周興、來俊臣之亞焉。 神龍初，隨例降爵，封耿國公，累轉懷州刺史，尋卒。 從父弟攸暨攸暨，則天伯父士讓孫也。 天授中，封士讓為楚王，攸暨封千乘郡王。 賜爵實封三百戶。 兄攸寧為建昌郡王，實封四百戶。 攸寧歷遷鳳閣侍郎、納言、冬官尚書，病卒。
By then many commoners who had been forced to follow the rebels were returning home. Yizong treated them all as rebels and had them killed. He even cut out their gall bladders while they were still alive; as the executions proceeded and blood pooled at his feet, he chatted and laughed as though nothing were amiss. Previously. Sun Wanrong's lieutenant He A-xiao had captured Jizhou and likewise slaughtered many men and women. By then people called Yizong and A-xiao the Two Hes, and a saying went: "Of all who kill, these Two Hes kill the most. " Yizong had also, since the Tianshou era, often received secret orders to conduct interrogations and control the prisons; kings, dukes, and great ministers were frequently framed and convicted through his hand. People regarded him as second only to Zhou Xing and Lai Junchen. At the beginning of the Shenlong era he was demoted by precedent to Duke of Geng, later served as Prefect of Huaizhou, and soon died. Youji, a younger male cousin on the shared grandfather's side, was the grandson of Zetian's paternal uncle Shirang. During Tianshou, Shirang was enfeoffed as King of Chu and Youji as Prince of Qiansheng. He received a noble title with an actual fief of three hundred households. His elder brother Youning was Prince of Jianchang with an actual fief of four hundred households. Youning served in turn as Vice Minister of the Phoenix Pavilion, Remonstrating Secretary, and Minister of the Winter Office, and died of illness.
46
攸暨初為右衛中郎將，尚太平公主，授駙馬都尉。 累遷右衛將軍，進封定王，又加實封三百戶。 俄又改安定郡王，歷遷司禮卿、左散騎常侍，加特進。 神龍中，拜司徒，復封定王，實封滿一千戶，固辭不拜。 尋而隨例降封樂壽郡王，拜右散騎常侍，加開府儀同三司。 延秀等誅後，又降封楚國公。 卒，贈太尉、并州大都督，追封定王。 尋以公主謀逆，令平毀其墓。
Youji was first Commandant of the Right Guard; he married Princess Taiping and was appointed Commandant of the Horse Guards. He rose to General of the Right Guard, was advanced to King Ding, and received three hundred additional actual fief households. Shortly afterward his title was changed to Prince of Anding; he served as Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and Left Regular Attendant of Cavalry, and was granted Special Advancement. During the Shenlong era he was appointed Minister of Education and again enfeoffed as King Ding with an actual fief of one thousand households, but he firmly declined. Shortly afterward, following precedent, he was demoted to Prince of Leshou, appointed Right Regular Attendant of Cavalry, and granted Honorary Grand General with the Presidency of the Department of State Affairs. After Yanxiu and the others were executed, he was demoted again to Duke of Chu. He died and was posthumously appointed Grand Commandant and Great Protector-General of Bingzhou, with posthumous enfeoffment as King Ding. Shortly afterward, when the princess plotted rebellion, the court ordered his tomb leveled and destroyed.

太平公主者，高宗少女也。 以則天所生，特承恩寵。 初，永隆年降駙馬薛紹。 紹，垂拱中被誣告與諸王連謀伏誅，則天私殺攸暨之妻以配主焉。 公主豐碩，方額廣頤，多權略，則天以為類己，每預謀議，宮禁嚴峻，事不令泄。 公主亦畏懼自檢，但崇飾邸第。 二十餘年，天下獨有太平一公主，父為帝，母為后，夫為親王，子為郡王，貴盛無比。 永淳已前朝制，親王食實封八百戶，有至一千戶； 公主出降三百戶，公主加五十戶。 太平食湯沐之邑一千二百戶，聖歷初加至三千戶。
Princess Taiping was Emperor Gaozong's youngest daughter. As Zetian's own daughter, she enjoyed exceptional favor. Early on, in the Yonglong era, she married Imperial Son-in-law Xue Shao. During Chuihong, Shao was falsely accused of plotting with various princes and executed; Zetian secretly had Youji's wife killed and gave her to the princess as a new match. The princess was imposing in build, with a square forehead and broad cheeks, and she was adept at intrigue. Zetian saw her as a kindred spirit and included her in every plot; palace security was tight and nothing was permitted to leak out. The princess, for her part, lived in cautious restraint and confined herself to lavishly outfitting her mansion. For more than twenty years, Princess Taiping alone in the empire could claim an emperor for a father, an empress for a mother, an imperial prince for a husband, and commandery princes for sons—wealth and rank beyond compare. Before Yongchun, court custom granted imperial princes actual fiefs of eight hundred households, with some reaching one thousand; princesses upon marriage received three hundred households, with an additional fifty for the princess title itself. Taiping held a ceremonial fief of twelve hundred households; at the start of Shenglì this rose to three thousand.
48
，預誅張易之謀有功，進號鎮國太平公主，相王加號安國相王，並食實封通前五千戶，賞賜不可勝紀。 公主孽氏二男二女，武氏二男一女，並食實封。 又相王、衛王重俊、成王千里宅，遣衛士宿衛，環其所居，十步置一仗舍，持兵巡僥，同於宮禁。 太平、長寧、安樂三公主，置鋪一如親王。 二年正月，置公主府。 ，公主男崇簡、崇敏、崇行，同授三品，與漁陽王兄弟四人同制。 時中宗仁善，韋后、上官昭容用事禁中，皆以為智謀不及公主，甚憚之。 公主日益豪橫，進達朝士，多至大官，詞人後進造其門者，或有貧窘，則遺之金帛，士亦翕然稱之。
For her part in the successful plot against Zhang Yizhi, her title was elevated to Pacifying-the-Realm Princess Taiping, and the Prince of Xiang was styled Pacifying-the-State Prince of Xiang; together they received actual fiefs of five thousand households counting earlier grants, and rewards beyond tallying. The princess's two sons and two daughters by concubines, together with two Wu-clan sons and one daughter, all held actual fiefs. Guards were also posted overnight at the mansions of the Prince of Xiang, Prince Wei Chongjun, and Prince Cheng Qianli, encircling their residences with a sentry booth every ten paces and armed patrols—matching palace security. Princesses Taiping, Changning, and Anle were given guard stations on the same model as imperial princes. In the first month of the second year, official princess households were established. Her sons Chongjian, Chongmin, and Chongxing were all given third rank together, under the same arrangement as the four Yuyang princes. Emperor Zhongzong was mild by nature; Empress Wei and Shangguan Zhaorong held sway inside the palace, but both judged themselves no match for the princess in wit and scheme, and feared her deeply. The princess grew ever more overbearing, advancing court officials—many to high office. When poets and rising talents visited her gate, the needy among them received gold and silk, and men of letters spoke of her with one voice in praise.
