及六月，韋后作逆稱制，偽尊溫王。 玄宗居臨淄邸，憤之，將清內難。 公主又預其謀，令男崇簡從之。 及立溫王，數日，天下之心歸於相府，難為其議。 公主入啟幼主，以王室多故，資於長君，乃提下幼主，因與玄宗、大臣尊立睿宗。 公主頻著大勛，益尊重，乃加實封五千戶，通前滿一萬戶。 公主子崇行、崇敏、崇簡三人，封異姓王； 崇行國子祭酒，四人九卿三品。 每入奏事，坐語移時，所言皆聽。 薦人或驟歷清職，或至南北衙將相，權移人主。 軍國大政，事必參決，如不朝謁，則宰臣就第議其可否。
In the sixth month, Empress Wei rebelled, assumed regency, and set up the Prince of Wen as a puppet ruler. Xuanzong, lodged at the Linzi mansion, burned with anger and prepared to resolve the crisis within the palace. The princess joined the plot as well, sending her son Chongjian to accompany him. Once the Prince of Wen was installed, within days public sentiment rallied to the Prince of Xiang, and the arrangement became untenable. The princess went in to advise the young emperor that the royal house was in turmoil and needed an elder, steady hand; she brought the boy down from the throne, and with Xuanzong and the chief ministers installed Ruizong. Having earned great merit repeatedly, the princess rose still higher in honor and received five thousand additional actual fief households, bringing her total to ten thousand. Her three sons—Chongxing, Chongmin, and Chongjian—were enfeoffed as kings of surname other than Li; Chongxing became Director of the National University; four of them held third-rank posts among the Nine Ministers. Each time she came in to report, she would sit in audience for hours, and whatever she proposed was accepted. Her recommendations could vault men into clean, high offices or into the chancellors and generals of both bureaus—the locus of power shifted away from the throne. On matters of army and state she had to be consulted; when she skipped court, chancellors came to her mansion to debate policy with her.
50
公主由是滋驕，田園遍於近甸膏腴，而市易造作器物，吳、蜀、嶺南供送，相屬於路。 綺疏寶帳，音樂輿乘，同於宮掖。 侍兒披羅綺，常數百人，蒼頭監嫗，必盈千數。 外州供狗馬玩好滋味，不可紀極。 有胡僧惠範，家富於財寶，善事權貴，公主與之私，奏為聖善寺主，加三品，封公，殖貨流於江劍。 公主懼玄宗英武，乃連結將相，專謀異計。 其時宰相七人，五出公主門，常元楷、李慈掌禁兵，常私謁公主。
From this the princess grew still more arrogant. Her estates spread across the fertile fields near the capital; for commerce and manufactured luxuries, Wu, Shu, and Lingnan sent goods in an unbroken stream along the roads. Carved silk screens, jeweled canopies, music, and equipages matched the inner palace. Hundreds of maids in gauze and brocade were always in attendance; male and female servants numbered more than a thousand. Outlying provinces sent dogs, horses, curios, and delicacies in quantities beyond count. A foreign monk named Huifan, immensely wealthy, cultivated the powerful; the princess took him as a lover and had him made abbot of Shengshan Temple, raised to third rank and enfeoffed as duke, while his trading interests spread through the Jiang and Jian regions. Fearing Xuanzong's martial spirit, the princess cultivated ties with chiefs and generals and plotted against him. Of the seven chancellors, five were her clients; Chang Yuankai and Li Ci commanded the palace guard and visited her privately on a regular basis.
51
七月，玄宗在武德殿，事漸危逼，乃勒兵誅其黨竇懷貞、蕭至忠、岑羲等，公主遽入山寺，數日方出，賜死於家。 公主諸子及黨與死者數十人。 籍其家，財貨山積，珍奇寶物，侔於御府，馬牧羊牧田園質庫，數年徵斂不盡。 惠範家產亦數十萬貫。 惟良子攸緒攸緒，惟良子也。 少有志行。 天授中封安平郡王，歷遷殿中監，出為揚州大都督府長史。 聖歷中，棄官隱於嵩山，以琴書藥餌為務。 中宗即位，以車安備禮徵之，降書曰：
In the seventh month, as matters at Wude Hall grew dangerously urgent, Xuanzong moved troops and executed her allies—Dou HuaiZhen, Xiao Zhizhong, Cen Xi, and others. The princess fled into a mountain monastery, did not emerge for several days, and was then granted death in her own house. Dozens of the princess's sons and associates perished with her. Her property was confiscated: wealth heaped like a mountain, curios rivaling the imperial treasury; horses, flocks, estates, and pawn offices yielded revenue for years that could not be fully collected. Huifan's estate as well came to several hundred thousand strings of cash. Youxu, son of Weiliang, was Weiliang's son. From youth he was known for integrity and purpose. During Tianshou he was enfeoffed Prince of Anping, rose to Director of the Palace Administration, and was appointed Chief Administrator of the Yangzhou Metropolitan Protectorate. During Shenglì he resigned his post and retired to Mount Song, devoting himself to the zither, books, and medicinal alchemy. When Zhongzong came to the throne, he was summoned with proper carriage and ceremonial honors; an imperial letter went out, saying:
52
攸緒應召至都，授太子賓客。 尋請歸嵩山，制從之，令京官五品已上餞送於定鼎門外。
Youxu answered the summons and came to the capital, where he was appointed Counselor to the Heir Apparent. He soon asked to return to Mount Song; the throne assented and ordered capital officials of fifth rank and above to escort him to a farewell outside Dingding Gate.
53
及三思、延秀等構逆，諸武多坐誅戮，唯攸緒以隱居不預其禍，時論美之。 睿宗即位，又降敕曰：「頃以賊臣結黨，后族擅權，扇動宮闈，肆行鴆毒。 靈祇所感，奸惡伏誅； 今得宗社乂安，天地交泰。 卿久厭簪紱，早慕林泉，守道不回，見幾而作，興言高尚，有足嘉稱。 但怒用不遷，罪無相及，為善有驗，卿之謂與！ 或慮驚疑，故令慰謝。 」其見重如此。 尋徵為太子賓客，不就。 ，攸緒又請就廬山居止，制不許。 仍令州縣數加存問，不令外人侵擾。 十一年卒，年六十九。 薛懷義薛懷義者，京兆鄠縣人，本姓馮，名小寶。 以鬻臺貨為業，偉形神，有膂力，為市於洛陽，得幸於千金公主侍兒。 公主知之，入宮言曰：「小寶有非常材用，可以近侍。 」因得召見，恩遇日深。 則天欲隱其跡，便於出入禁中，乃度為僧。 又以懷義非士族，乃改姓薛，令與太平公主婿薛紹合族，令紹以季父事之。 自是與洛陽大德僧法明、處一、惠儼、稜行、感德、感知、靜軌、宣政等在內道場念誦。 懷義出入乘廄馬，中官侍從，諸武朝貴，匍匐禮謁，人間呼為薛師。
When Sansi, Yanxiu, and others plotted treason and most of the Wu clan were executed, Youxu alone escaped calamity through his reclusion, and public opinion applauded him. When Ruizong took the throne, another edict proclaimed: "Lately villainous ministers formed cliques, the empress's kin seized power, stirred turmoil in the inner palace, and poison ran freely. Moved by the spirits, the wicked have been brought low and executed; the altars of state are at peace and Heaven and Earth are in harmony again. You long ago wearied of rank and ribbon, and early turned toward mountain and stream; you held to the Way without wavering, acted when the moment was right, and your lofty withdrawal deserves every praise. Though offenders were punished without leniency, guilt does not extend by association; virtue brings its own reward—and you are proof of it! Fearing you might be alarmed or unsettled, we send this message of reassurance. " Such was the esteem in which he was held. He was soon summoned again as Counselor to the Heir Apparent but declined. Youxu then asked to take up residence on Mount Lu, but the throne refused. The court still ordered local officials to inquire after him regularly and forbade outsiders to disturb him. In the eleventh year he died, at the age of sixty-nine. Xue Huaiyi was a native of Hu County in Jingzhao; his original surname was Feng and his given name Xiaobao. He made his living as a market trader; imposing in build and strong of limb, he did business in Luoyang and won the favor of a maid in Princess Qianjin's household. When the princess learned of this, she went into the palace and said, "Xiaobao has extraordinary gifts and is fit for close attendance. " He was summoned to audience, and favor deepened day by day. Zetian wished to conceal his movements and ease his access to the inner palace, so she had him ordained as a monk. Because Huaiyi was not of the gentry, she changed his surname to Xue, had him incorporated into the clan of Princess Taiping's son-in-law Xue Shao, and ordered Shao to treat him as a younger paternal uncle. Thereafter he joined the great Luoyang monks Faming, Chuyi, Huiyan, Lengxing, Gande, GanZhi, Jinggui, and Xuanzheng in sutra recitation at the inner dharma hall. Huaiyi rode imperial stable horses when he went abroad, attended by eunuchs; Wu clansmen and court grandees prostrated themselves before him, and people called him Master Xue.
54
垂拱初，說則天於故洛陽城西修故白馬寺，懷義自護作。 寺成，自為寺主。 頗恃恩狂蹶，其下犯法，人不敢言。 右臺御史馮思勖屢以法劾之； 懷義遇勖於途，令從者毆之，幾死。 又於建春門內敬愛寺別造殿宇，改名佛授記寺。
At the start of Chuihong he persuaded Zetian to restore the old White Horse Temple west of Luoyang, and Huaiyi personally supervised the work. When the temple was finished, he installed himself as abbot. He grew arrogant on imperial favor; when his followers broke the law, no one dared report it. Right Censorate Investigating Censor Feng Sijiu repeatedly impeached him under the law; Huaiyi met Sijiu on the road and had his followers beat him nearly to death. He also built separate halls within Jing'ai Temple inside Jianchun Gate and renamed it Foshouji Temple.
55
，拆乾元殿，於其地造明堂，懷義充使督作。 凡役數萬人，曳一大木千人，置號頭，頭一㘚，千人齊和。 明堂大屋凡三層，計高二百尺。 又於明堂北起天堂，廣袤亞於明堂。 懷義以功拜左威衛大將軍，封梁國公。
The Qianyuan Hall was demolished and the Bright Hall erected on the site, with Huaiyi appointed commissioner to supervise construction. Tens of thousands of laborers were pressed into service; a thousand men were needed to haul each great timber, with chant leaders appointed so that one call from the leader brought a thousand voices in unison. The Bright Hall rose in three tiers to a height of two hundred feet. North of the Bright Hall they also raised the Heavenly Hall, slightly smaller in breadth and length. For this work Huaiyi was appointed General of the Left Weiwu Guard and enfeoffed as Duke of Liang.
56
永昌中，突厥默啜犯邊，以懷義為清平道大總管，率軍擊之，至單於臺，刻石紀功而還。 加輔國大將軍，進右衛大將軍，改封鄂國公、柱國，賜帛二千段。
During Yongchang, when the Türk Mo-ch'o raided the frontier, Huaiyi was made Grand Commander of the Qingping Circuit, led troops against him, reached Chanyu Terrace, carved a stone record of his achievement, and returned. He was further made Assistant State General and General of the Right Guard, enfeoffed as Duke of E and Pillar of State, and granted two thousand bolts of silk.
57
懷義與法明等造《大雲經》，陳符命，言則天是彌勒下生，作閻浮提主，唐氏合微。 故則天革命稱周，懷義與法明等九人並封縣公，賜物有差，皆賜紫袈娑、銀龜袋。 其偽《大雲經》頒於天下寺，各藏一本，令升高座講說。 則天將革命，誅殺宗屬諸王，唯千金公主以巧媚善進奉獨存； 抗疏請以則天為母，因得曲加恩寵，改邑號為延安大長公主，加實封，賜姓武氏。 以子克乂娶魏王武承嗣女，內門參問，不限早晚，見則盡歡。
Huaiyi and Faming and others fabricated the Great Cloud Sutra, proclaiming portents that Zetian was Maitreya reborn, sovereign of Jambudvīpa, and that the Tang line was fated to decline. When Zetian changed the dynasty and styled herself Zhou, Huaiyi, Faming, and seven others—all nine of them—were enfeoffed as commandery dukes, given gifts in varying measure, and awarded purple monastic robes and silver tortoise pouches. The forged Great Cloud Sutra was distributed to every temple in the realm, each to keep one copy and expound it from the high seat. As Zetian prepared to change the dynasty, she executed the imperial clansmen and princes; only Princess Qianjin survived, through artful flattery and lavish offerings; she submitted a memorial asking to take Zetian as her mother, and thereby won special favor: her title was changed to Great Princess of Yan'an, her actual fief was increased, and she was granted the surname Wu. Her son Keyi married the daughter of Prince Wei Wu Chengsi, and visits at the inner gate were permitted at any hour; whenever they met, the revelry ran its full course.
58
，默啜復犯塞，又以懷義為代北道行軍大總管，以李多祚、蘇宏暉為將。 未行，改朔方道行軍大總管，以內史李昭德為行軍長史，鳳閣侍郎、平章事蘇味道為行軍司馬，契苾明、曹仁師、沙咤忠義等十八將軍以討之。 未行虜退，乃止。
When Mo-ch'o again raided the frontier, Huaiyi was again made Grand Military Commander of the Daibei Circuit, with Li Duozuo and Su Honghui as his generals. Before he marched, his appointment was changed to Grand Military Commander of the Shuofang Circuit, with Palace Secretary Li Zhaode as campaign chief administrator, Vice Minister of the Phoenix Pavilion and Grand Councilor Su Weidao as campaign vice marshal, and eighteen generals including Qibi Ming, Cao Renshi, and Shazha Zhongyi to subdue the enemy. Before the army marched, the enemy withdrew, and the campaign was called off.
59
懷義後厭入宮中，多居白馬寺，刺血畫大像，選有膂力白丁度為僧，數滿千人。 侍御史周矩疑其奸，奏請劾之，不許。 固請之，則天曰：「卿且退，朕即令去。 」矩至臺，薛師亦至，乘馬蹋階而下，便坦腹於床。 矩召臺吏，將按之，遽乘馬而去。 矩具以聞，則天曰：「此道人風病，不可苦問。 所度僧任卿勘當。 」矩按之，窮其狀以聞，諸僧悉配遠州。 遷矩天官員外郎，竟為薛師所構，下獄，免官。
Huaiyi later grew weary of the palace and spent most of his time at White Horse Temple, pricking his blood to paint a great image and ordaining strong commoners as monks until their number reached a thousand. Attending Censor Zhou Ju suspected wrongdoing and memorialized for an investigation, but the request was denied. When he pressed the matter, Zetian said, "Withdraw for now—I shall have him come to you at once. Ju returned to the censorate, and Master Xue arrived as well—riding his horse down the steps and then sprawling bare-bellied on a couch. Ju summoned the censorate clerks to investigate, but Huaiyi suddenly mounted his horse and rode off. Ju reported everything; Zetian said, "This monk suffers from wind disorder and cannot be pressed with hard questioning. As for the monks he ordained, you may investigate and adjudicate as you see fit. Ju investigated, reported the full findings, and all the monks were banished to distant prefectures. Ju was promoted to Vice Director in the Ministry of Celestial Offices, but in the end Master Xue framed him; he was imprisoned and dismissed from office.
60
後有御醫沈南璆得幸，薛師恩漸衰，恨怒頗甚。 證聖中，乃焚明堂、天堂，並為灰燼，則天愧而隱之，又令懷義充使督作。 乃於明堂下置九州鼎，鑄銅為十二屬形象，置於本辰位，皆高一丈，懷義率人作號頭安置之。
Later the imperial physician Shen Nanqiu won the empress's favor; Master Xue's influence faded, and his resentment burned ever hotter. During Zhengsheng he set fire to the Bright Hall and Heavenly Hall and reduced them to ashes. Zetian was ashamed and hushed the matter up, then again appointed Huaiyi commissioner to supervise the rebuilding. Below the Bright Hall they placed the Nine Provinces cauldrons, cast bronze into images of the Twelve Branches, and set them in their proper celestial positions, each a full zhang in height; Huaiyi led the laborers as chant leaders to hoist them into place.
61
其後益驕倨，則天惡之，令太平公主擇膂力婦人數十，密防慮之。 人有發其陰謀者，太平公主乳母張夫人令壯士縛而縊殺之，以輦車載屍送白馬寺。 其侍者僧徒，皆流竄遠惡處。
He grew ever more arrogant, and Zetian came to loathe him. She had Princess Taiping choose several dozen strong women to keep secret watch over him. When someone exposed his secret plots, Princess Taiping's wet nurse Lady Zhang had brawny men bind and strangle him, then sent his corpse by palanquin to White Horse Temple. His attendants and monk followers were all banished to remote and harsh regions.
62
=韋溫=
Wei Wen
63
韋溫，中宗韋庶人從父兄也。 父玄儼，高宗末官至許州刺史。 玄儼弟玄貞，初為普州參軍，以女為皇太子妃，擢拜豫州刺史。 中宗嗣位，妃為后。 及帝降為廬陵王，玄貞配流欽州而死。 后母崔氏，為欽州首領寧承兄弟所殺。
Wei Wen was the paternal cousin of Emperor Zhongzong's Consort Wei. His father Xuanyan, in the final years of Gaozong's reign, rose to Prefect of Xuzhou. Xuanyan's younger brother Xuanzhen had begun as a military adjutant in Puzhou; when his daughter became the crown prince's consort, he was promoted to Prefect of Yuzhou. When Zhongzong succeeded to the throne, the consort became empress. When the emperor was demoted to Prince of Luling, Xuanzhen was exiled to Qinzhou and died there. The empress's mother, Lady Cui, was killed by the brothers Ning Cheng, local chieftains of Qinzhou.
64
玄貞有四子：洵、浩、洞、泚，亦死於容州。 后二妹，逃竄獲免，間行歸長安。
Xuanzhen had four sons—Xun, Hao, Dong, and Ci—who also died in Rongzhou. The empress's two younger sisters fled, escaped with their lives, and made their way back to Chang'an by secret routes.
65
及中宗復位，韋氏復為皇后。 其日，追贈玄貞為上洛郡王。 左拾遺賈虛己上疏諫曰：「孔子曰：『惟名與器，不可以假人。 』且非李氏而王，自古盟書所棄。 今陛下創制謀始，垂範將來，為皇王令圖，子孫明鏡。 匡復未幾，后族有私，臣雖庸愚，尚知未可； 史官執簡，必是直書。 今萬姓颙然，聞一善令，莫不途歌里頌，延頸向風，欣然慕化，日恐不及。 陛下奈何行私惠，使樵夫議之。 即先朝贈太原王，殷鑒不遠。 同雲生於膚寸，尋木起於蘗栽，誠可惜也。 渙汗既行，難改成命，臣望請皇后抗表固辭，使天下知弘讓之風，彤管著沖謙之德，是則巍巍聖鑒，無得而稱。 」疏奏不省。
When Zhongzong regained the throne, the Wei clan's daughter was again made empress. That same day Xuanzhen was posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Shangluo. Left Reminder of Omissions Jia Xuji submitted a memorial of remonstrance, saying, "Confucius said, 'Titles and instruments of office must not be lent to others.' "Moreover, to enfeoff one not of the Li clan as king has been rejected in oaths since antiquity. Your Majesty is now founding institutions and laying plans that will set a model for future generations—a bright charter for kings and emperors, a mirror for your descendants. Not long after restoration, the empress's clan is already receiving private favors; though I am dull and ignorant, I still know this cannot be right; The historiographers who hold the bamboo slips will surely record it truthfully. The myriad people now look up with hope; at one good decree they sing it on the roads and praise it in their lanes, craning their necks toward the breeze, gladly yearning for reform, fearing each day they will not receive enough. How can Your Majesty grant private favors and let woodcutters discuss them? The recent precedent of enfeoffing the Prince of Taiyuan in the previous reign is a warning not far off. Clouds that bring rain rise from a finger's breadth; a towering tree springs from a stump—this would truly be a pity. Since the decree has already been issued and is hard to revoke, I hope the empress may submit a memorial firmly declining it, so all under Heaven will know the spirit of magnanimous yielding, and the red brush will record her modest virtue—then Your Majesty's august judgment would be beyond praise. The memorial was submitted but received no response.
66
尋又追贈玄貞為太師、雍州牧、益州大都督； 玄儼為特進、并州大都督、魯國公。 遣使迎玄貞及崔氏喪柩歸京師。 又遣廣州都督周仁軌率兵討斬寧承兄弟，以其首祭於崔氏。 擢拜仁軌左羽林大將軍，賜爵汝南郡公，食實封五百戶。 及玄貞等柩將至，上與后登長樂宮，望喪而泣。 加贈玄貞為酆王，謚曰文獻，仍號其廟曰褒德，陵曰榮先。 各置官員，並給戶一百人守衛灑掃。 又贈玄貞子洵為吏部尚書、汝南郡王，浩太常卿、武陵郡王，洞衛尉卿、淮南郡王，泚太僕卿、上蔡郡王，亦遣使迎其喪柩於京師。
Shortly afterward Xuanzhen was again posthumously given the titles Grand Mentor, Governor of Yongzhou, and Great Protector-General of Yizhou; Xuanyan was made Special Advancement, Great Protector-General of Bingzhou, and Duke of Lu. Envoys were sent to bring the coffins of Xuanzhen and Lady Cui home to the capital. Guangzhou Protector-General Zhou Rengui was also dispatched with troops to pursue and behead the brothers Ning Cheng, offering their heads in sacrifice before Lady Cui. Zhou Rengui was promoted to General of the Left Yulin Guard, enfeoffed as Duke of Runan, and granted an actual fief of five hundred households. As the coffins of Xuanzhen and the others were about to arrive, the emperor and empress ascended Changle Palace, gazing toward the funeral procession and weeping. Xuanzhen received further posthumous honors as Prince of Feng, with posthumous title Wenxian; his temple was named Baoerde and his tomb Rongxian. Officials were appointed for each, and one hundred households were assigned to guard and maintain them. Xuanzhen's sons were also posthumously honored: Xun as Minister of the Civil Service and Prince of Runan; Hao as Minister of Ceremonial and Prince of Wuling; Dong as Minister of the Guard and Prince of Huainan; Ci as Minister of the Stud and Prince of Shangcai—and envoys were sent to bring their coffins to the capital.
67
溫，神龍中累遷禮部尚書，封魯國公。 弟湑，左羽林將軍，封曹國公。 后妹夫陸頌為國子祭酒，馮太和為太常少卿，太和尋卒，又適嗣虢王邕。 湑子捷，尚成安公主，溫從祖弟濯，尚定安公主，皆拜駙馬都尉。
During Shenlong, Wen was repeatedly promoted to Minister of Rites and enfeoffed Duke of Lu. His younger brother Xu was General of the Left Yulin Guard and Duke of Cao. The empress's brother-in-law Lu Song was Director of the National University; Feng Taihe was Vice Minister of Ceremonies—Taihe soon died, and she remarried Heir of Prince Guo Yong. Xu's son Jie married Princess Cheng'an; Wen's distant cousin Zhuo married Princess Ding'an; both were appointed Imperial Son-in-Law Commandants.
68
，溫遷太子少保、同中書門下三品，仍遙授揚州大都督。 溫等既居榮要，燻灼朝野，時人比之武氏。 湑及陸頌相次病卒，賻贈甚厚。 及中宗崩，后令溫總知內外兵馬，守援宮掖。 又引從子播、族弟璇、弟捷、濯等，分掌屯營及左右羽林軍。 臨淄王討韋氏，溫等皆坐斬，宗族無少長皆死，語在《韋庶人傳》。 睿宗即位，仍令削平玄貞及洵等墳墓。
Wen was promoted to Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent and Co-signer of the Chancellery of the Three Departments, while also receiving the nominal appointment of Great Protector-General of Yangzhou. Once Wen and his kin held exalted and critical posts, their splendor eclipsed court and realm; contemporaries compared them to the Wu clan. Xu and Lu Song died of illness in succession, and funeral gifts were lavish. When Zhongzong died, the empress ordered Wen to take overall command of inner and outer military forces and guard the palace precincts. She also brought in her nephew Bo, clan cousin Xuan, younger brother Jie, Zhuo, and others to divide command of encampment garrisons and the Left and Right Yulin Armies. When the Prince of Linzi suppressed the Wei clan, Wen and the rest were all executed; none of the clan, young or old, survived—the account is given in the Biography of Consort Wei. When Ruizong took the throne, he ordered the tombs of Xuanzhen, Xun, and the others leveled.
69
=王仁皎=
Wang Renjiao
70
王仁皎，玄宗王庶人父也。 景龍中，官至長上果毅。 玄宗即位，以后父，歷將作大匠、太僕卿，遷開府儀同三司，封祁國公。 仁皎不預朝政，但厚自奉養，積子女財貨而已。 卒，贈太尉，官供葬事。 柩車既發，上於望春亭遙望之，令張說為其碑文，玄宗親書石焉。 子守一。
Wang Renjiao was the father of Emperor Xuanzong's Consort Wang. During Jinglong he reached the rank of Senior Commander of the Changshang Guard. When Xuanzong ascended the throne, as the empress's father he served successively as Director of Imperial Construction and Minister of the Stud, then was made Honorary Grand Master with the status of the Three Highest Offices and enfeoffed Duke of Qi. Renjiao took no part in governance but lived in lavish self-indulgence, amassing wealth for his sons and daughters—that was all. He died and was posthumously appointed Grand Commandant; the state provided his funeral. When the funeral procession set out, the emperor watched from afar at Wangchun Pavilion, had Zhang Yue compose his epitaph, and Xuanzong personally inscribed the stone. Son: Shouyi.
71
守一與后雙生。 守一與玄宗有舊，及上登極，以清陽公主妻之。 從討蕭至忠、岑羲等有功，自尚乘奉御遷殿中少監，特封晉國公，累轉太子少保。 父卒，襲爵祁國公。 十一年，坐與庶人潛通左道，左遷柳州司馬，行至藍田驛，賜死。 守一性貪鄙，積財巨萬，及籍沒其家，財帛不可勝計。
Shouyi and the empress were twins. Shouyi had long standing with Xuanzong; when the emperor took the throne, he gave him Princess Qingyang in marriage. For merit in the campaign against Xiao Zhizhong, Cen Xi, and others, he rose from Chief Groom of the Imperial Carriage to Vice Director of the Palace Administration, was specially enfeoffed Duke of Jin, and was eventually promoted to Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent. When his father died, he inherited the title Duke of Qi. In the eleventh year, for secretly practicing heterodox arts with the deposed consort, he was demoted to Military Assistant of Liuzhou; on reaching Lantian post station he was granted death. Shouyi was greedy and base by nature and amassed wealth in the tens of thousands; when his household was confiscated, goods and cash beyond reckoning were found.
72
=吳溆=
Wu Xu
73
吳溆，章敬皇后之弟也，濮州濮陽人。 祖神泉，位終縣令。 父令珪，益州郫縣丞。 ，代宗始封拜外族，贈神泉司徒，令珪太尉，令珪母弟前宣城令令瑤為開府儀同三司、太子家令，封濮陽郡公； 中郎將令瑜為開府儀同三司、太子諭德、濟陽郡公。 漵時為盛王府錄事參軍，拜開府儀同三司、太子詹事、濮陽郡公。 以元舅遷鴻臚少卿、金吾將軍。 建中初，遷大將軍。 漵雖居戚屬，恭遜謙和，人皆重之。
Wu Xu was the younger brother of Empress Zhangjing, a native of Puyang in Puzhou. His grandfather Shenquan ended his career as county magistrate. His father Lingui was assistant magistrate of Pi County in Yizhou. When Daizong first began enfeoffing maternal kin, Shenquan was posthumously made Director of the Masses, Lingui Grand Commandant, and Lingui's younger maternal half-brother the former magistrate of Xuancheng Lingyao was made Honorary Grand Master with the status of the Three Highest Offices and Director of the Heir Apparent's Household, enfeoffed Duke of Puyang; Middle General Lingyu was made Honorary Grand Master with the status of the Three Highest Offices, Mentor of the Heir Apparent, and Duke of Jiyang. At the time Xu was Recording Officer of the Shengwang mansion; he was appointed Honorary Grand Master with the status of the Three Highest Offices, Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent, and Duke of Puyang. As chief maternal uncle he was transferred to Vice Minister of State Ceremonials and General of the Gold Crow Guard. At the start of Jianzhong he was promoted to Grand General. Though Xu held imperial kinship, he was deferential, modest, and courteous, and all held him in esteem.
74
涇師之亂，從幸奉天，盧杞、白志貞謂德宗曰：「臣細觀硃泚心跡，必不至為戎首，佇當效順。 宜擇大臣一人，入京師慰諭，以觀其心。 」上召從幸群臣言之，皆憚其行。 漵起奏曰：「不以臣才望無堪，臣願北行。 」德宗甚悅。 漵退而謂人曰：「人臣食君之祿，死君之難，臨危自計，非忠也。 吾忝戚屬，今日委身於賊，誠知必死，不欲聖情慊於無人犯難也。 」即日賫詔見泚，深陳上待屬之意。 時泚逆謀已定，貌雖從命，而心已異，乃留漵於客省，竟被害。 上聞之，悲悼不已，贈太子太傅，賜其家實封二百戶，一子五品正員官，敕收城日葬事官給。 弟湊。
During the Jingyuan mutiny, he accompanied the emperor to Fengtian. Lu Qi and Bai Zhizhen said to Dezong, "We have closely observed Zhu Ci's intentions; he will surely not take the lead in rebellion and will soon submit." Choose one chief minister to enter the capital and reassure him, to test his heart. The emperor summoned the officials who had accompanied him and put the matter before them; all feared to go. Xu rose and memorialized, "Do not mind that I lack talent and standing—I am willing to go north. Dezong was greatly pleased. Xu withdrew and said to others, "A minister who eats his lord's stipend ought to die in his lord's peril; to calculate one's own safety at a crisis is not loyalty. I bear the shame of imperial kinship; today I throw myself into the rebel's hands. I know I shall surely die, but I do not wish the sacred heart to be vexed that no one would brave the peril. That same day he carried the edict to see Zhu Ci and spoke at length of the emperor's regard for the imperial kin. By then Zhu Ci's treacherous designs were fixed; though he outwardly obeyed, inwardly his heart had already turned, and he detained Xu in the guest hall, where Xu was ultimately killed. When the emperor heard of it, he mourned without end, posthumously appointing Xu Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent, granting his family an actual fief of two hundred households, one son a regular fifth-rank office, and ordering that when the capital was recovered the state would provide the funeral. Younger brother: Cou.
75
湊，寶歷中與兄漵同日開府，授太子詹事，俱封濮陽郡公。 湊以兄弟三品，固辭太過，乞授卑官。 乃以湊檢校太子賓客，兼太子家令，充十宅王使。 累轉左金吾衛大將軍。
Cou, in Baoli, on the same day as his elder brother Xu received the opening of an honorary mansion and was appointed Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent; both were enfeoffed Duke of Puyang. Cou, considering it excessive that both brothers held third rank, firmly declined and requested a lesser appointment. He was then made Acting Counselor to the Heir Apparent, concurrently Director of the Heir Apparent's Household, and Commissioner for the Ten Princely Residences. He was successively transferred to Grand General of the Left Jinwu Guard.
76
湊小心謹慎，智識周敏，特承顧問，偏見委信。 大歷中，滑帥令狐彰、汴帥田神功相次歿於理所，時籓方兵驕，乘戎帥喪亡，人情多梗。 代宗命湊銜命撫慰，至必委曲說諭，隨所欲為之奏請，皆得軍民和協，帝深重之。
Cou was cautious and prudent, quick and thorough in judgment, and received special consultation and partial trust. During Dali, Hu Lingzhang, military commissioner of Hua, and Tian Shen'gong, military commissioner of Bian, died in succession at their posts; frontier armies were arrogant, and with the commanders' deaths popular sentiment grew restless in many places. Daizong ordered Cou to go on imperial commission to reassure them; wherever he arrived he tactfully persuaded and memorialized for whatever they desired, achieving harmony between armies and people; the emperor valued him deeply.
77
宰臣元載弄權，招致賄賂，醜跡日彰。 帝惡之，將加之法，恐左右泄漏，無與言者，唯與湊密計圖之。 及收載於內侍省，同列王縉，其黨楊炎、王昂、韓洄、包佶、韓會等，皆當從坐籍沒。 湊諫救百端，言「法宜從寬，縉等從坐，理不至死。 若不降以等差，一例極刑，恐虧損聖德。 」由是縉等得減死，流貶之。
Chancellor Yuan Zai manipulated power, solicited bribes, and his shameful conduct grew more conspicuous day by day. The emperor hated him and intended to punish him by law, but feared leaks among those close at hand and had no one to speak with—he confided only in Cou to plan it. When Zai was arrested in the Inner Palace Service, his colleague Wang Jin and his partisans Yang Yan, Wang Ang, Han Hui, Bao Ji, Han Hui, and others were all subject to guilt by association and confiscation. Cou remonstrated at length in their defense, saying, "The law should be applied with lenience; Wang Jin and the others, guilty by association, do not deserve death in principle. If distinctions in punishment are not granted and all receive the extreme penalty alike, I fear the sacred virtue will be diminished. Thereby Wang Jin and the rest had their death sentences commuted and were banished.
78
大歷末，丁繼母喪免。 建中初，起為右衛將軍，兼通州刺史。 貞元初，入為太子賓客，出為福州刺史、御史中丞、福建觀察使。 為政勤儉清苦，美譽日聞。 宰相竇參以私怨惡之，數加譖毀，又言湊風病，不任趨馳。 德宗召湊至京師，對於別殿，上令殿上行走，以驗其病否，由是悟參之誣，因是惡參。 尋以湊為陜州大都督府長史、陜虢觀察使，以代參之黨李翼。 會劉玄佐卒，以湊檢校兵部尚書、汴州刺史、御史大夫、宣武軍節度使。
At the end of Dali he was dismissed to observe mourning for his stepmother. At the start of Jianzhong he was recalled as General of the Right Guard, concurrently Prefect of Tongzhou. At the start of Zhenyuan he entered court as Counselor to the Heir Apparent, then went out as Prefect of Fuzhou, Vice Censor-in-Chief, and Military Commissioner of Fujian. In governing he was diligent, frugal, and austere, and his good reputation spread day by day. Chancellor Dou Can bore him a private grudge and repeatedly slandered him, claiming moreover that Cou suffered a paralytic affliction and could not keep up with the duties that required him to hurry to and fro. Dezong summoned Cou to the capital and received him in a side hall, ordering him to walk back and forth across the hall to test whether he was truly ill. Thereby the emperor saw through Can's false accusation and turned against him. Soon afterward Cou was made Chief Administrator of the Shanzhou Superior Prefecture and Military Commissioner of Shan-Guo, replacing Li Yi, a partisan of Can. When Liu Xuanzuo died, Cou was appointed Acting Minister of War, Prefect of Bianzhou, Censor-in-Chief, and Military Commissioner of the Xuanwu Army.
79
時汴州軍亂，殺牙將曹金岸、縣令李邁，謀立玄佐子士寧。 上將遣兵送湊赴鎮，召宰臣議。 竇參深沮其行，恐軍中拒命，乃召湊回，授右金吾衛大將軍，而以梁宋節鉞授士寧。
At the time the Bianzhou army was in revolt. The mutineers killed the yabing general Cao Jin'an and the magistrate Li Mai and plotted to install Xuanzuo's son Shining as commander. The emperor was about to dispatch troops to escort Cou to his post and summoned the chief ministers to counsel him. Dou Can strongly opposed the move, fearing the army would refuse to obey. He had Cou recalled and appointed Grand General of the Right Jinwu Guard, while the military commission over Liang and Song was given to Shining instead.
80
春夏旱，穀貴，人多流亡。 京兆尹韓臯以政事不理黜官。 上召湊，面授京兆尹，即日令視事，經宿方下制。 湊孜孜為理，以勤儉為務，人樂其政。 時宮中選內官買物於市，倚勢強買物，不充價，人畏而避之，呼為「宮市」。 掌賦者多與中貴人交結假借，不言其弊。 湊為京尹，便殿從容論之，曰：「物議以中人買物於市，稍不便於人，此事甚細，虛掇流議。 凡宮中所須，責臣可辦，不必更差中使。 若以臣府縣外吏，不合預聞宮中所須，則乞選內官年高謹重者，充宮市令，庶息人間論議。 」又奏：「掌閑彍騎、飛龍內園、芙蓉及禁軍諸司等使，雜供手力資課太多，量宜減省。 」上多從之。
Drought struck in spring and summer; grain prices soared, and many people fled their homes. Han Gao, Metropolitan Governor of Jingzhao, was dismissed for mismanaging the administration. The emperor summoned Cou and personally appointed him Metropolitan Governor of Jingzhao. That same day Cou was ordered to take up his duties; the formal edict was not issued until the following day. Cou governed with tireless diligence and made thrift his watchword; the people welcomed his rule. At the time the palace sent eunuchs into the markets to buy goods. Leaning on their authority, they forced purchases and paid less than fair price. People feared them and kept out of their way, calling the practice the "Palace Market." Most revenue officials cultivated ties with powerful eunuchs and borrowed their influence, and none spoke of the abuse. As metropolitan governor, Cou raised the matter at leisure in the informal hall, saying, "Public opinion holds that eunuchs buying goods in the market is somewhat inconvenient for the people. The matter is very minor and needlessly stirs loose talk. Whatever the palace requires, your subject can supply it; there is no need to send eunuch envoys again. If, as a prefectural official outside the palace, I am not fit to be told what the palace needs, then I beg that older, sober eunuchs be chosen to serve as Palace Market commissioners, so that public complaint may cease. " He also memorialized: "The commissioners of the Palace Leisure Archery Cavalry, the Inner Garden Flying Dragon Office, the Hibiscus Office, and the various offices of the Palace Army levy too many miscellaneous labor-service fees and contributions; these should be reduced as appropriate. The emperor largely followed his recommendations.
81
初，府掾吏以湊起自戚籓，不諳簿領，凡有疑獄難決之事，多候湊將出時方呈，冀免指擿瑕病。 湊雖倉卒閱視，必指其奸幸之處，下筆決斷，無毫厘之差。 掾吏非大過，不行笞責； 而召面按問，詰責而釋之。 吏尤惕厲，庶務咸舉。
At first the prefectural clerks, thinking Cou had risen from imperial kin in a frontier post and was unfamiliar with ledgers and documents, would wait until he was about to leave before presenting doubtful cases that were hard to decide, hoping to escape having their errors exposed. Even when he reviewed them in haste, Cou always pinpointed where fraud and favoritism lay, wrote his decision, and never missed by the slightest margin. For clerks who had not committed grave offenses he did not impose flogging; instead he summoned them for face-to-face questioning, rebuked them, and let them go. The clerks became especially vigilant, and all routine affairs were properly handled.
82
文敬太子、義章公主相繼薨歿，上深追念，葬送之儀頗厚。 召集工役，載土築墳，妨民農務。 湊候上顧問，極言之。 宗屬門吏以湊論諫太繁，恐上厭苦，每以簡約規之。 湊曰：「聖上明哲，憂勞四海，必不以公主、太子之鐘念而忽疲民。 但人多順旨不言，若再三啟諫，必動宸情，則生民受賜。 長吏不言，是為阿旨。 如窮民上訴，罪在何人？ 」議者重之。 以能政，兼兵部尚書。 官街樹缺，所司植榆以補之，湊曰：「榆非九衢之玩。 」亟命易之以槐。 及槐陰成而湊卒，人指樹而懷之。
Crown Prince Wenjing and Princess Yizhang died in succession. The emperor mourned them deeply, and the rites of burial and send-off were quite lavish. Laborers were summoned to haul earth and build tombs, disrupting the people's farm work. When the emperor turned to him for counsel, Cou spoke out fully. The gate officials of the imperial kin, fearing that Cou's remonstrances were too frequent and would weary the emperor, often urged him to be brief. Cou said, "The sage sovereign is clear-sighted and toils for all under Heaven. He surely will not, out of lingering grief for the princess and crown prince, heedlessly exhaust the people. But many people simply agree with the sovereign's wishes and say nothing. If one remonstrates again and again, the imperial heart will surely be moved, and the common people will receive the benefit. For a chief official not to speak is to curry favor with the sovereign's wishes. If the poor people appeal in complaint, upon whom will the guilt fall? Commentators respected this. Because of his capable administration, he was additionally appointed Minister of War. Where trees were missing on the official avenues, the responsible offices planted elms to fill the gaps. Cou said, "Elms are not fit ornament for the capital's main thoroughfares. He immediately ordered them replaced with pagoda trees. By the time the pagoda trees cast shade, Cou had died; people pointed to the trees and cherished his memory.
83
湊於德宗為老舅，漢魏故事，多退居散地，才免罪戾而已。 湊自貞元已來，特承恩顧，歷中外顯貴，雖聖獎隆深，亦由湊小心辦事，奉職有方故也。
Cou was Dezong's elder maternal uncle. By Han and Wei precedent, such kin mostly retired to honorific posts and barely escaped guilt and punishment. From Zhenyuan onward Cou received special imperial favor and held prominent posts at court and in the provinces. Though the emperor's commendation was deep and generous, it was also because Cou was careful in handling affairs and performed his duties with method.
84
湊既疾，不召巫醫，藥不入口，家人泣而勉之。 對曰：「吾以凡才，濫因外戚進用，起家便授三品，歷顯位四十年，壽登七十，為人足矣，更欲何求？ 古之以親戚進用者，罕有善終，吾得歸全以侍先人，幸也。 」德宗知之，令御醫進藥，不獲已，服之。 四月卒，時年七十一，贈尚書左僕射，罷朝一日。
Once Cou fell ill, he would summon neither shamans nor physicians. Medicine did not pass his lips, and his family wept as they urged him to take it. He replied, "With my ordinary talent I was improperly promoted through imperial kinship. From the start of my career I was granted third rank, held prominent posts for forty years, and have reached seventy years of life — as a man I have had enough. What more could I seek? Of those promoted through kinship in antiquity, few ended well. That I may die whole and attend my forebears is good fortune. When Dezong learned of this, he ordered the imperial physician to present medicine. Unable to refuse, Cou took it. He died in the fourth month at the age of seventy-one. He was posthumously appointed Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, and court was suspended for one day.
85
=竇覦=
Dou Di
86
竇覦，昭成皇后族侄。 父光，華原尉。 覦以親廕，釋褐右衛率府兵曹參軍。 鄜坊節度臧希讓奏為判官，累授監察殿中侍御史、檢校工部員外郎、坊州刺史。 ，討李懷光於河中，詔覦以坊州兵七百人屯邰陽。 賊平，以功兼御史中丞。 遷同州刺史，入朝為戶部侍郎。
Dou Di was a clansman nephew of Empress Zhaocheng. His father Guang was Assistant Magistrate of Huayuan. Di entered service through kinship privilege and upon first appointment became Army Staff Officer of the Right Guard Commandant's Office. Zang Xirang, military commissioner of Fufang, memorialized to appoint him judge. He was successively appointed Supervising Censor, Palace Censor, Acting Vice Minister of Works, and Prefect of Fangzhou. When campaigning against Li Huaiguang at Hezhong, an edict ordered Di to garrison seven hundred Fangzhou troops at Heyang. When the rebels were pacified, he was additionally appointed Vice Censor-in-Chief for his merit. He was transferred to Prefect of Tongzhou, then entered court as Vice Minister of Revenue.
87
覦無他才伎，為吏有計數，又以韓滉子婿，故籓府辟召，遂歷牧守。 宰相竇參，覦再從侄。 參少依覦，及參秉政，力薦於朝，故有貳卿之拜。 數月，為揚州大都督府長史、御史大夫、充淮南節度副大使、知節度事，既非德舉，人咸薄之。 赴鎮旬日，暴卒，詔贈禮部尚書。
Di had no other talent or skill, but as an official he was shrewd in calculation. Moreover, as son-in-law of Han Huang, he was recruited by frontier headquarters and thus rose through governorships. Chancellor Dou Can was Di's second cousin once removed. Can in youth had relied on Di, and once Can held power he vigorously recommended him at court; hence the appointment to a vice-ministerial post. Within a few months he was made Chief Administrator of the Yangzhou Superior Prefecture, Censor-in-Chief, Deputy Military Commissioner of Huainan, and Acting Military Commissioner. Since this was not a promotion based on merit, all looked down on him. Within ten days of reaching his post he died suddenly. An edict posthumously appointed him Minister of Rites.
88
=柳晟=
Liu Sheng
89
柳晟者，肅宗皇后之甥。 母和政公主。 父潭，官至太僕卿、駙馬都尉。 晟少無檢操，代宗於諸甥之中，特加撫鞠，俾與太子、諸王同學，授詩書，恩寵罕比。 累試太常卿。
Liu Sheng was a nephew of Suzong's empress. His mother was Princess Hezheng. His father Tan rose to Grand Master of the Stud and Commandant Escort of the Son-in-Law. Sheng in youth lacked restraint in conduct. Among all his nephews Daizong singled him out for special nurturing, had him study together with the crown prince and the princes, and taught him the classics. His favor was rarely matched. He was repeatedly appointed Minister of Ceremonies.
90
德宗即位，以與晟幼同硯席，尤親之。 涇師之亂，從幸奉天，晟密啟曰：「願受詔入京城，遊說群賊，冀其攜貳。 」德宗壯而許之。 晟與賊帥多有舊，出入其門說誘之。 事泄，為硃泚所擒，械之於獄。 晟有力，乃於獄中穿垣破械而遁，落發為僧，間道歸行在。 遷將作少監。 元和初，檢校工部尚書、興元尹、山南西道節度使。 罷鎮入朝，以違詔進奉，為御史元稹所劾，詔宥之。 俄充入回鶻冊立使，復命，遷左金吾衛大將軍。 卒，贈太子少保。
When Dezong acceded, because he had shared desk and mat with Sheng in youth, he was especially close to him. During the Jingshi mutiny, following the emperor's flight to Fengtian, Sheng secretly memorialized, saying, "I wish to receive an edict to enter the capital, persuade the rebel bands, and hope to make them waver and divide. Dezong admired this and granted his request. Sheng had old ties with many of the rebel chiefs and went in and out of their gates to persuade and entice them. When the affair was exposed, he was seized by Zhu Ci and fettered in prison. Sheng was strong. He tunneled through the prison wall, broke his fetters, and escaped. He shaved his head and became a monk, then by hidden paths returned to the imperial camp. He was promoted to Vice Director of the Directorate of Imperial Construction. At the start of Yuanhe he was made Acting Minister of Works, Governor of Xingyuan, and Military Commissioner of Shannan West Circuit. When he left his post and entered court, he was impeached by the censor Yuan Zhen for presenting tribute in violation of an edict. An edict pardoned him. Soon he served as envoy to the Uighurs to invest their ruler. Upon his return he was promoted to Grand General of the Left Jinwu Guard. He died and was posthumously appointed Junior Mentor to the Heir Apparent.
91
=王子顏=
Wang Ziyan
92
王子顏，瑯邪臨沂人，莊憲皇后之父也。 祖思敬，少從軍，累試太子賓客。 父難得，有勇決，善騎射，天寶初為河源軍使。 吐蕃贊普王子郎支都有勇，乘諳真馬，寶鈿裝鞍，出陣求鬥，無敢與校者。 難得挾槍奮馬突前，刺殺郎支都，斬其首，傳於京師。 軍還，玄宗召見之，令於殿前乘馬挾槍作刺郎支都之狀。 賜以錦袍金帶，累拜金吾將軍同正員。
Wang Ziyan, a native of Linyi in Langye, was the father of Empress Zhuangxian. His grandfather Sijing entered the army in youth and was repeatedly appointed Counselor to the Heir Apparent. His father Nan'de was brave and resolute and skilled in horsemanship and archery. At the start of Tianbao he was commissioner of the Heyuan Army. Langzhidu, a son of the Tibetan tsenpo, was brave. Riding the horse Anzhen with a jeweled saddle, he came out to the battle line seeking combat, and none dared to match him. Nan'de grasped his lance, spurred his horse forward in a rush, stabbed and killed Langzhidu, cut off his head, and sent it to the capital. When the army returned, Xuanzong summoned him and ordered him to ride before the hall, lance in hand, and act out the thrust that killed Langzhidu. He was granted a brocade robe and gold belt and was successively appointed Regular Assistant General of the Jinwu Guard.
93
，從哥舒翰擊吐蕃於積石，虜吐谷渾王子悉弄參及子婿悉頰藏而還，累拜左武衛將軍、關西遊奕使。 九載，擊吐蕃，收五橋，拔樹敦城，補白水軍使。 十三載，從收九曲，加特進。
He followed Geshu Han to attack the Tibetans at Jishi, captured the Tuyuhun prince Sinong Can and his son-in-law Sinuocang, and returned. He was successively appointed General of the Left Martial Guard and Commissioner of the Guanxi Mobile Corps. In the ninth year he attacked the Tibetans, recovered Wuqiao, captured Shudun city, and was appointed commissioner of the Baishui Army. In the thirteenth year he followed in the recovery of the Nine Bends and was granted the special advancement.
94
祿山之叛，從哥舒翰戰於潼關； 關門不守，從肅宗幸靈武。 時行在闕軍賞，難得進絹三千疋及金銀器等。 至德初，試衛尉卿、興平軍使，兼鳳翔都知兵馬使。 進收京城，與賊軍戰。 其下靳元曜戰酣墮馬，難得馳救之，賊射之中眉，皮穿披下鄣目。 難得自拔去箭，並皮掣洛，馳馬復戰，血流被面，而抗賊不已。 肅宗深嘉之。 從郭子儀攻安慶緒於相州，累封瑯邪郡公，英武軍使。 卒，贈潞州大都督。
When Lushan rebelled, he followed Geshu Han to fight at Tong Pass; when the pass was not held, he followed Suzong in the flight to Lingwu. At the time the imperial camp lacked funds for military rewards. Nan'de presented three thousand bolts of silk and gold and silver vessels. At the start of Zhide he was appointed Minister of the Guard, commissioner of the Xingping Army, and concurrently Commander of Military Affairs at Fengxiang. Advancing to recover the capital, he fought the rebel army. His subordinate Jin Yuanyao, in the heat of battle, fell from his horse. Nan'de galloped to rescue him, and the rebels shot him in the brow. The skin was pierced and hung down over the cheek guard before his eyes. Nan'de himself pulled out the arrow, tore away the hanging skin, spurred his horse and fought again. Blood covered his face, yet he resisted the rebels without cease. Suzong deeply commended him. He followed Guo Ziyi in attacking An Qingxu at Xiangzhou and was successively enfeoffed Duke of Langye and made commissioner of the Yingwu Army. He died and was posthumously appointed Governor-General of Luzhou.
95
子顏少從父征役，累官金紫光祿大夫、檢校衛尉卿，生后而卒。 順宗內禪，以后生憲宗皇帝，褒贈先代：思敬司徒，難得太傅，子顏太師。
Ziyan from youth followed his father on campaigns, rose to Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon and Acting Minister of the Guard, and died after the empress was born. When Shunzong abdicated internally and the empress had borne Emperor Xianzong, earlier generations were honored posthumously: Sijing was made Minister over the Masses, Nan'de Grand Tutor, and Ziyan Grand Preceptor.
96
顏子重榮，官至福王傅； 用，官至太子賓客、金吾將軍。
Ziyan's son Zhongrong rose to Tutor to the Prince of Fu; Yong rose to Counselor to the Heir Apparent and General of the Jinwu Guard.
97
贊曰：戚里之賢，避寵畏權。 不恤禍患，鮮能保全。 福盈者敗，勢壓者顛。 武之惟良，明於自然。
Comment: Among the virtuous of the imperial kin, they shunned favor and feared power. Those who did not spare themselves from calamity — few could preserve themselves intact. Those whose fortune runs full are ruined; those whose power presses too hard are overturned. Of the Wu clan, Weiliang alone understood how nature works.
